cuptiActivityEnable.doc:
Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record.

Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record. Multiple kinds can be enabled by calling this function multiple times. By default all activity kinds are disabled for collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if the activity kind cannot be enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if the activity kind is not supported.

cuptiActivityEnableAllSyncRecords.doc:
Enables collecting records for all synchronization operations.

CUPTI provides CUDA event query and stream query records via [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_SYNCHRONIZATION`]. Using this API, CUPTI client can disable to record CUDA event query and stream query records for queries for which the operations have not yet been completed on the CUDA event/stream.

By default, the record is generated for all CUDA events and stream irrespective of whether the operations have been completed on the CUDA event/stream.

cuptiActivityEnableAllocationSource.doc:
Enables tracking the source library for memory allocation requests.

This API is used to control whether or not we track the source library of memory allocation requests. Default value is 0, i.e. it is not tracked. The activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_MEMORY2`] needs to be enabled, and if this flag is set, we get the full path of the shared object responsible for the GPU memory allocation request in the member source in the [CUpti_ActivityMemory4](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__ActivityMemory4.html#structcupti__activitymemory4) records. Also note that this feature adds runtime overhead.

cuptiActivityEnableAndDump.doc:
Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record.

For certain activity kinds it dumps existing records.

In general, the behavior of this API is similar to the API [cuptiActivityEnable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga348cf81393b39ab2f89604aaaa8defc2) i.e. it enables the collection of a specific kind of activity record. Additionally, this API can help in dumping the records for activities which happened in the past before enabling the corresponding activity kind. The API allows to get records for the current resource allocations done in CUDA For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DEVICE`], existing device records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONTEXT`], existing context records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_STREAM`], existing stream records are dumped For CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_ NVLINK, existing NVLINK records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_PCIE`], existing PCIE records are dumped For other activities, the behavior is similar to the API [cuptiActivityEnable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga348cf81393b39ab2f89604aaaa8defc2)

Device records are emitted in CUPTI on CUDA driver initialization. Those records can only be retrieved by the user if CUPTI is attached before CUDA initialization. Context and stream records are emitted on context and stream creation. The use case of the API is to provide the records for CUDA resources (contexts/streams/devices) that are currently active if user late attaches CUPTI.

Before calling this function, the user must register buffer callbacks to get the activity records by calling [cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga237e2401b0ce69dcb265b1f9079f0b65). If the user does not register the buffers and calls API [cuptiActivityEnableAndDump](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga12080fe6fdacf80869db472e41b98027), then CUPTI will enable the activity kind but not provide any records for that activity kind.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if the activity kind cannot be enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if the activity kind is not supported.

cuptiActivityEnableAndDump_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityEnableAndDump_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_ActivityKind kind, CUpti_ActivityConfig * activityConfig)
cuptiActivityEnableAndDump_v2.doc:
Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record.

For certain activity kinds it dumps existing records.

In general, the behavior of this API is similar to the API [cuptiActivityEnable_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga563584d948863ce4d7688847096149d2) i.e. it enables the collection of a specific kind of activity record. Additionally, this API can help in dumping the records for activities which happened in the past before enabling the corresponding activity kind. The API allows to get records for the current resource allocations done in CUDA For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DEVICE`], existing device records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONTEXT`], existing context records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_STREAM`], existing stream records are dumped For CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_ NVLINK, existing NVLINK records are dumped For [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_PCIE`], existing PCIE records are dumped For other activities, the behavior is similar to the API [cuptiActivityEnable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga348cf81393b39ab2f89604aaaa8defc2)

Device records are emitted in CUPTI on CUDA driver initialization. Those records can only be retrieved by the user if CUPTI is attached before CUDA initialization. Context and stream records are emitted on context and stream creation. The use case of the API is to provide the records for CUDA resources (contexts/streams/devices) that are currently active if user late attaches CUPTI.

Before calling this function, the user must register buffer callbacks to get the activity records by calling [cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gacbe1ba1b75f76472038cb2fd34d84e09). If the user does not register the buffers and calls API [cuptiActivityEnableAndDump_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga3303f9ceb4eb1d604f00985badb3c7ea), then CUPTI will enable the activity kind but not provide any records for that activity kind.

kind.doc: The kind of activity record to collect.

activityConfig.doc: The activity config. It can be NULL.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if the activity kind cannot be enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if the activity kind is not supported.

cuptiActivityEnableContext.doc:
Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record for a context.

Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record for a context. This setting done by this API will supersede the global settings for activity records enabled by [cuptiActivityEnable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga348cf81393b39ab2f89604aaaa8defc2). Multiple kinds can be enabled by calling this function multiple times.

context.doc: The context for which activity is to be enabled.

kind.doc: The kind of activity record to collect.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if the activity kind cannot be enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if the activity kind is not supported.

cuptiActivityEnableCudaEventDeviceTimest.doc:
Enable/Disable collecting device timestamp for [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CUDA_EVENT`] record.

CUPTI provides device timestamps via ‘deviceTimestamp’ field in [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CUDA_EVENT`] records. Using this API, CUPTI client can enable or disable the collection of CUDA event device timestamps. By default, the collection of CUDA event device timestamps is disabled.

cuptiActivityEnableDeviceGraph.doc:
Controls the collection of records for device launched graphs.

This API is used to control the collection of records for device launched graphs. Default value is 0, i.e. these records are not collected. This API needs to be called before initialization of CUDA and this setting should not be changed during the profiling session.

cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi.doc:
Controls the collection of activity records for specific CUDA Driver APIs.

Activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DRIVER`] controls the collection of either all CUDA Driver APIs or none. API cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi can be used for fine-grained control, it allows enabling/disabling tracing of a specific set of CUDA Driver APIs. To disable collection of a small set of CUDA Driver APIs, user can first enable the collection of all Driver APIs using the activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DRIVER`] and call this API to disable specific Driver APIs. And to enable the collection of a small set of CUDA Driver APIs, user can call this API without using the activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DRIVER`].

Note: Activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_DRIVER`] overrides the settings done by this API if it is called after the API.

cbid.doc: callback id of the CUDA Driver API. This can be found in the header cupti_driver_cbid.h.

enable.doc: is a boolean, denoting whether to enable or disable the collection.

cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_CallbackId cbid, uint8_t enable)
cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi_v2.doc:
Controls the collection of activity records for specific CUDA Driver APIs for a given subscriber.

This is the per-subscriber version of [cuptiActivityEnableDriverApi](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gaada27f148dd634f0c7466db1cb2a6a78). It allows each subscriber to independently enable or disable tracing of specific CUDA Driver APIs.

subscriber.doc: Handle to the subscriber. Must have been previously created via [cuptiSubscribe_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__CALLBACK__API.html#group__cupti__callback__api_1ga817004c126bedadf956162f20de18491).

cbid.doc: callback id of the CUDA Driver API.

enable.doc: is a boolean, denoting whether to enable or disable the collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if the subscriber handle is invalid or cbid is out of range.

cuptiActivityEnableHWTrace.doc:
Enables CUDA kernel timestamp collection via Hardware Event System (HES).

This API enables hardware-based collection of CUDA kernel timestamps as an alternative to the traditional software instrumentation and semaphore-based approach. HES-based collection provides lower overhead and more accurate timing measurements.

This API must be called after CUDA driver initialization but before creating the CUDA context. As a generic solution, this API can be called from the [`CUpti_CallbackIdResource::CUPTI_CBID_RESOURCE_CU_INIT_FINISHED`] callback. Once enabled, HES-based tracing persists for the entire profiling session and cannot be disabled.

This API can also be called before CUDA driver initialization. After driver initialization, CUPTI may switch to traditional semaphore-based tracing and return error through callback with domain [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_STATE`] if HES-based tracing cannot be supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: if HW trace cannot be enabled on the current platform.

cuptiActivityEnableLatencyTimestamps.doc:
Controls the collection of queued and submitted timestamps for kernels.

This API is used to control the collection of queued and submitted timestamps for kernels whose records are provided through the struct [CUpti_ActivityKernel12](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__ActivityKernel12.html#structcupti__activitykernel12). Default value is 0, i.e. these timestamps are not collected. This API needs to be called before initialization of CUDA and this setting should not be changed during the profiling session.

This API is not supported if the HW trace is enabled through the API [cuptiActivityEnableHWTrace](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gaa8f1642a87b1ef876014c766e798f534).

cuptiActivityEnableLaunchAttributes.doc:
Controls the collection of launch attributes for kernels.

This API is used to control the collection of launch attributes for kernels whose records are provided through the struct [CUpti_ActivityKernel12](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__ActivityKernel12.html#structcupti__activitykernel12). Default value is 0, i.e. these attributes are not collected.

cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi.doc:
Controls the collection of activity records for specific CUDA Runtime APIs.

Activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME`] controls the collection of either all CUDA Runtime APIs or none. API cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi can be used for fine-grained control, it allows enabling/disabling tracing of a specific set of CUDA Runtime APIs. To disable collection of a small set of CUDA Runtime APIs, user can first enable the collection of all Runtime APIs using the activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME`] and call this API to disable specific Runtime APIs. And to enable the collection of a small set of CUDA Runtime APIs, user can call this API without using the activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME`].

Note: Activity kind [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME`] overrides the settings done by this API if it is called after the API.

cbid.doc: callback id of the CUDA Runtime API. This can be found in the header cupti_runtime_cbid.h.

enable.doc: is a boolean, denoting whether to enable or disable the collection.

cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_CallbackId cbid, uint8_t enable)
cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi_v2.doc:
Controls the collection of activity records for specific CUDA Runtime APIs for a given subscriber.

This is the per-subscriber version of [cuptiActivityEnableRuntimeApi](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gaaad5fd7a8f998e475588623eb65dac9a). It allows each subscriber to independently enable or disable tracing of specific CUDA Runtime APIs.

subscriber.doc: Handle to the subscriber. Must have been previously created via [cuptiSubscribe_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__CALLBACK__API.html#group__cupti__callback__api_1ga817004c126bedadf956162f20de18491).

cbid.doc: callback id of the CUDA Runtime API.

enable.doc: is a boolean, denoting whether to enable or disable the collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if the subscriber handle is invalid or cbid is out of range.

cuptiActivityEnable_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityEnable_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_ActivityKind kind, CUpti_ActivityConfig * pActivityConfig)
cuptiActivityEnable_v2.doc:
Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record for the subscriber.

Enable collection of a specific kind of activity record. Multiple kinds can be enabled by calling this function multiple times. By default all activity kinds are disabled for collection.

kind.doc: The kind of activity record to collect.

pActivityConfig.doc: The activity config. It can be NULL.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if the activity kind cannot be enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if the activity kind is not supported.

cuptiActivityFlush.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityFlush(CUcontext context, uint32_t streamId, uint32_t flag)
cuptiActivityFlush.doc:
Wait for all activity records to be delivered via the completion callback.

This function does not return until all activity records associated with the specified context/stream are returned to the CUPTI client using the callback registered in cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks. To ensure that all activity records are complete, the requested stream(s), if any, are synchronized.

If `context` is NULL, the global activity records (i.e. those not associated with a particular stream) are flushed (in this case no streams are synchronized). If `context` is a valid CUcontext and `streamId` is 0, the buffers of all streams of this context are flushed. Otherwise, the buffers of the specified stream in this context is flushed.

Before calling this function, the buffer handling callback api must be activated by calling cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.

**DEPRECATED** This method is deprecated CONTEXT and STREAMID will be ignored. Use cuptiActivityFlushAll to flush all data.

streamId.doc: The stream ID.

flag.doc: The flag can be set to indicate a forced flush. See CUpti_ActivityFlag.

CUPTI_ERROR_CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATIO.doc: if not preceded by a successful call to cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.

cuptiActivityFlushAll.doc:
Request to deliver activity records via the buffer completion callback.

This function returns the activity records associated with all contexts/streams (and the global buffers not associated with any stream) to the CUPTI client using the callback registered in cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.

This is a blocking call but it doesn’t issue any CUDA synchronization calls implicitly thus it’s not guaranteed that all activities are completed on the underlying devices. Activity record is considered as completed if it has all the information filled up including the timestamps if any. It is the client’s responsibility to issue necessary CUDA synchronization calls before calling this function if all activity records with complete information are expected to be delivered.

Behavior of the function based on the input flag: (-)::For default flush i.e. when flag is set as 0, it returns all the activity buffers which have all the activity records completed, buffers need not to be full though. It doesn’t return buffers which have one or more incomplete records. Default flush can be done at a regular interval in a separate thread. (-)::For forced flush i.e. when flag [`CUpti_ActivityFlag::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_FLAG_FLUSH_FORCED`] is passed to the function, it returns all the activity buffers including the ones which have one or more incomplete activity records. It’s suggested for clients to do the force flush before the termination of the profiling session to allow remaining buffers to be delivered. In general, it can be done in the at-exit handler.

Before calling this function, the buffer handling callback api must be activated by calling cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.

When multiple subscribers are allowed, the buffers of all subscribers are flushed with the same flag. It is not possible to flush the buffers of only a specific subscriber.

See also

[cuptiActivityFlushPeriod](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gaded430c34c6b7dbf935377c65c7d6491).

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if not preceded by a successful call to cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.

cuptiActivityFlushPeriod.doc:
Sets the flush period for the worker thread.

CUPTI creates a worker thread to minimize the perturbance for the application created threads. CUPTI offloads certain operations from the application threads to the worker thread, this includes synchronization of profiling resources between host and device, delivery of the activity buffers to the client using the callback registered in cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks. For performance reasons, CUPTI wakes up the worker thread based on certain heuristics.

This API is used to control the flush period of the worker thread. This setting will override the CUPTI heuristics. Setting time to zero disables the periodic flush and restores the default behavior.

Periodic flush can return only those activity buffers which are full and have all the activity records completed.

It’s allowed to use the API [cuptiActivityFlushAll](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gabae7160b2db7e97247a0d23812e373eb) to flush the data on-demand, even when client sets the periodic flush.

See also

[cuptiActivityFlushAll](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gabae7160b2db7e97247a0d23812e373eb).

cuptiActivityGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetAttribute(CUpti_ActivityAttribute attr, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiActivityGetAttribute.doc:
Read an activity API attribute.

Read an activity API attribute and return it in `*value`. In case of multiple subscribers, use cuptiActivityGetAttribute_v2 to read the attribute for the subscriber.

valueSize.doc: Size of buffer pointed by the value, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

value.doc: Returns the value of the attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attr` is not an activity attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: Indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiActivityGetAttribute_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetAttribute_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_ActivityAttribute attr, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiActivityGetAttribute_v2.doc:
Read an activity API attribute.

This function is similar to cuptiActivityGetAttribute. Note that in case of multiple subscribers, only cuptiActivityGetAttribute_v2 can be used to read the attribute for the subscriber.

Read an activity API attribute and return it in `*value`.

valueSize.doc: Size of buffer pointed by the value, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

value.doc: Returns the value of the attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attr` is not an activity attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: Indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiActivityGetEnabledKinds.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetEnabledKinds(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_ActivityKind * buffer, uint32_t * bufferSize, uint32_t * enabledKindsCount)
cuptiActivityGetEnabledKinds.doc: Get the enabled activity kinds for a subscriber.

subscriber.doc: The subscriber handle. If NULL, the union of activity kinds enabled across all subscribers is returned.

buffer.doc: The buffer to store the enabled activity kinds. If NULL, the number of enabled activity kinds is returned in `enabledKindsCount`.

bufferSize.doc: The size of the buffer. If NULL, only the number of enabled activity kinds is returned in `enabledKindsCount`. If NULL and `buffer` is not NULL, [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`] is returned.

enabledKindsCount.doc: The number of enabled activity kinds. If NULL, [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`] is returned.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `enabledKindsCount` is NULL or if `subscriber` is invalid.

cuptiActivityGetNextRecord.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetNextRecord(uint8_t * buffer, size_t validBufferSizeBytes, CUpti_Activity * * record)

record.doc: Inputs the previous record returned by cuptiActivityGetNextRecord and returns the next activity record from the buffer. If input value is NULL, returns the first activity record in the buffer. Records of certain kinds like [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL`] may contain invalid (0) timestamps, indicating that no timing information could be collected for lack of device memory.

validBufferSizeBytes.doc: The number of valid bytes in the buffer.

CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED.doc: if no more records in the buffer.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if activity record is either incomplete or invalid.

cuptiActivityGetNextRecord_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetNextRecord_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, uint8_t * buffer, size_t validBufferSizeBytes, CUpti_Activity * * record)

subscriber.doc: Handle to the subscriber whose record layout should be used.

validBufferSizeBytes.doc: The number of valid bytes in the buffer.

record.doc: Inputs the previous record returned by cuptiActivityGetNextRecord_v2 and returns the next activity record from the buffer. If input value is NULL, returns the first activity record in the buffer.

CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED.doc: if no more records in the buffer.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_KIND.doc: if activity record is either incomplete or invalid.

cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords(CUcontext context, uint32_t streamId, size_t * dropped)
cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords.doc:
Get the number of activity records that were dropped of insufficient buffer space.

Get the number of records that were dropped because of insufficient buffer space. The dropped count includes records that could not be recorded because CUPTI did not have activity buffer space available for the record (because the CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc callback did not return an empty buffer of sufficient size) and also CDP records that could not be record because the device-size buffer was full (size is controlled by the [`CUpti_ActivityAttribute::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_DEVICE_BUFFER_SIZE_CDP`] attribute). The dropped count maintained for the queue is reset to zero when this function is called.

context.doc: The context, or NULL to get dropped count from global queue.

streamId.doc: The stream ID.

dropped.doc: The number of records that were dropped since the last call to this function.

cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUcontext context, uint32_t streamId, size_t * dropped)
cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords_v2.doc:
Get the number of dropped activity records for a specific subscriber.

This is the per-subscriber version of [cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga496d13eb1f4f4fcce37ce3f3434c5e4a).

streamId.doc: Stream ID (reserved for future use).

dropped.doc: Returns the number of dropped records.

cuptiActivityGetStructSize.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityGetStructSize(CUpti_ActivityKind activityKind, uint32_t version, size_t * activityStructSize)
cuptiActivityGetStructSize.doc:
Get the size of the activity struct for a given CUPTI version.

This API is applicable only for predefined activity structs.

activityKind.doc: The activity kind to get the size for.

activityStructSize.doc: The size of the activity struct.

version.doc: The version of the CUPTI API. If 0, returns size for current version. If non-zero, returns size for the specified version. The version format is xxyyzz, e.g., 130000 for CUPTI 13.0, 130100 for CUPTI 13.1. The version of CUPTI can be queried using cuptiGetVersion API. Only versions >= 130000 are supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: if `version` is non-zero and is less than 130000.

cuptiActivityPopExternalCorrelationId.doc:
Pop an external correlation id for the calling thread.

This function notifies CUPTI that the calling thread is leaving an external API region.

cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks.doc:
Registers callback functions with CUPTI for activity buffer handling.

This function registers two callback functions to be used in asynchronous buffer handling. If registered, activity record buffers are handled using asynchronous requested/completed callbacks from CUPTI.

Registering these callbacks prevents the client from using CUPTI’s blocking enqueue/dequeue functions.

funcBufferRequested.doc: callback which is invoked when an empty buffer is requested by CUPTI.

funcBufferCompleted.doc: callback which is invoked when a buffer containing activity records is available from CUPTI.

cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle subscriber, CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc_v2 funcBufferRequested, CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc_v2 funcBufferCompleted)
cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks_v2.doc:
Registers callback functions with CUPTI for activity buffer handling for the subscriber.

This function registers two callback functions to be used in asynchronous buffer handling. If registered, activity record buffers are handled using asynchronous requested/completed callbacks from CUPTI.

Registering these callbacks prevents the client from using CUPTI’s blocking enqueue/dequeue functions.

funcBufferRequested.doc: callback which is invoked when an empty buffer is requested by CUPTI.

funcBufferCompleted.doc: callback which is invoked when a buffer containing activity records is available from CUPTI.

cuptiActivityRegisterTimestampCallback.doc:
Registers callback function with CUPTI for providing timestamp.

This function registers a callback function to obtain timestamp of user’s choice instead of using CUPTI provided timestamp. By default CUPTI uses different methods, based on the underlying platform, to retrieve the timestamp Linux (x86_64, aarch64 sbsa, aarch64) uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) Windows uses QueryPerformanceCounter() WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) as CLOCK_REALTIME can cause backward jumps. QNX uses ClockCycles() Timestamps retrieved using these methods are converted to nanosecond if needed before usage.

Timestamps for GPU activities such as kernels, memory copies and memset operations are recorded directly on the GPU. To provide a unified and normalized view of these timestamps in relation to CPU time, CUPTI performs a linear interpolation to convert GPU timestamps into CPU timestamps during post-processing. For activities where timestamps are captured on the GPU, the timestamp callback is invoked during the post-processing phase, while converting GPU timestamps into CPU timestamps. For activities for which timestamps are captured directly on the CPU, the timestamp callback is invoked immediately at the time of the activity.

The registration of timestamp callback should be done before any of the CUPTI activity kinds are enabled to make sure that all the records report the timestamp using the callback function registered through cuptiActivityRegisterTimestampCallback API.

Changing the timestamp callback function in CUPTI through cuptiActivityRegisterTimestampCallback API in the middle of the profiling session can cause records generated prior to the change to report timestamps through previous timestamp method.

cuptiComputeCapabilitySupported.doc:
Check support for a compute capability.

This function is used to check the support for a device based on it’s compute capability. It sets the `support` when the compute capability is supported by the current version of CUPTI, and clears it otherwise. This version of CUPTI might not support all GPUs sharing the same compute capability. It is suggested to use API [cuptiDeviceSupported](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga2493c952b9ceccf953ade5a6816fefdb) which provides correct information.

See also

[cuptiDeviceSupported](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga2493c952b9ceccf953ade5a6816fefdb).

major.doc: The major revision number of the compute capability.

minor.doc: The minor revision number of the compute capability.

support.doc: Pointer to an integer to return the support status.

cuptiDeviceSupported.doc:
Check support for a compute device.

This function is used to check the support for a compute device. It sets the `support` when the device is supported by the current version of CUPTI, and clears it otherwise.

See also

[cuptiComputeCapabilitySupported](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga22c5ce610ffbf5940b7c05be54fc813d).

cuptiGetAutoBoostState.doc:
Get auto boost state.

The profiling results can be inconsistent in case auto boost is enabled. CUPTI tries to disable auto boost while profiling. It can fail to disable in cases where user does not have the permissions or CUDA_AUTO_BOOST env variable is set. The function can be used to query whether auto boost is enabled.

cuptiGetTimestamp.doc:
Get the CUPTI timestamp.

Returns a timestamp normalized to correspond with the start and end timestamps reported in the CUPTI activity records. The timestamp is reported in nanoseconds.

cuptiGetTimestamp_v2.doc:
Get the CUPTI timestamp (API currently in beta).

If a subscriber registers a particular timestamp callback, this API will use that callback to get the timestamp. In CUDA 13.3, this will fall back to [cuptiGetTimestamp()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga7d8294c686b5293237a6daae8eae3dde). In future versions, this will provide the timestamp callback registered by the requesting subscriber, and fallback to [cuptiGetTimestamp()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga7d8294c686b5293237a6daae8eae3dde) if no callback is registered.

Returns a timestamp normalized to correspond with the start and end timestamps reported in the CUPTI activity records. The timestamp is reported in nanoseconds.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `timestamp` is NULL or `subscriber` is NULL.

cuptiIsTracingSessionRunning.doc:
Check whether a CUPTI tracing session is still running.

This API returns true if a CUPTI library is already loaded by another CUPTI user by using any CUPTI API. This API returns false when CUPTI is finalized and there is no CUPTI currently loaded and active. Can be used to determine if it is safe to unload your CUPTI based tool. Note that this API itself does not load the CUPTI library, it merely checks if a CUPTI library is already loaded by another CUPTI user.

cuptiSetThreadIdType.doc:
Set the thread-id type.

CUPTI uses the method corresponding to set type to generate the thread-id. See enum [CUpti_ActivityThreadIdType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gac6fcebeb84a89d8f1862d31338efd4c5) for the list of methods. Activity records having thread-id field contain the same value. Thread id type must not be changed during the profiling session to avoid thread-id value mismatch across activity records. This API is not supported when multiple subscribers are allowed. Use the corresponding attribute instead: [`CUpti_ActivityAttribute::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_THREAD_ID_TYPE`].

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: if `type` is not supported on the platform.

CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc)(CUcontext context, uint32_t streamId, uint8_t * buffer, size_t size, size_t validSize)
CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc.doc:
Function type for callback used by CUPTI to return a buffer of activity records.

This callback function returns to the CUPTI client a buffer containing activity records. The buffer contains `validSize` bytes of activity records which should be read using cuptiActivityGetNextRecord. The number of dropped records can be read using cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords. After this call CUPTI relinquished ownership of the buffer and will not use it anymore. The client may return the buffer to CUPTI using the CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc callback. Note: CUDA 6.0 onwards, all buffers returned by this callback are global buffers i.e. there is no context/stream specific buffer. User needs to parse the global buffer to extract the context/stream specific activity records.

fields.Param context: The context this buffer is associated with. If NULL, the buffer is associated with the global activities. This field is deprecated as of CUDA 6.0 and will always be NULL.
fields.Param streamId: The stream id this buffer is associated with. This field is deprecated as of CUDA 6.0 and will always be NULL.
fields.Param size: The total size of the buffer in bytes as set in CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc.
fields.Param validSize: The number of valid bytes in the buffer.

CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc_v2.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc_v2)(uint8_t * buffer, size_t size, size_t validSize, CUpti_BufferCallbackCompleteInfo * pBufferCompleteInfo)
CUpti_BuffersCallbackCompleteFunc_v2.doc:
Function type for callback used by CUPTI to return a buffer of activity records.

This callback function returns to the CUPTI client a buffer containing activity records. The buffer contains `validSize` bytes of activity records which should be read using cuptiActivityGetNextRecord. The number of dropped records can be read using cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords. After this call CUPTI relinquished ownership of the buffer and will not use it anymore. The client may return the buffer to CUPTI using the CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc callback. Note: CUDA 6.0 onwards, all buffers returned by this callback are global buffers i.e. there is no context/stream specific buffer. User needs to parse the global buffer to extract the context/stream specific activity records.

fields.Param size: The total size of the buffer in bytes as set in CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc.
fields.Param validSize: The number of valid bytes in the buffer.
fields.Param pBufferCompleteInfo: Additional information about the completed buffer.

CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc)(uint8_t * * buffer, size_t * size, size_t * maxNumRecords)
CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc.doc:
Function type for callback used by CUPTI to request an empty buffer for storing activity records.

This callback function signals the CUPTI client that an activity buffer is needed by CUPTI. The activity buffer is used by CUPTI to store activity records. The callback function can decline the request by setting `*buffer` to NULL. In this case CUPTI may drop activity records.

fields.Param buffer: Returns the new buffer. If set to NULL then no buffer is returned.
fields.Param size: Returns the size of the returned buffer.
fields.Param maxNumRecords: Returns the maximum number of records that should be placed in the buffer. If 0 then the buffer is filled with as many records as possible. If > 0 the buffer is filled with at most that many records before it is returned.

CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc_v2.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc_v2)(uint8_t * * buffer, size_t * size, size_t * maxNumRecords, CUpti_BufferCallbackRequestInfo * pBufferRequestInfo)
CUpti_BuffersCallbackRequestFunc_v2.doc:
Function type for callback used by CUPTI to request an empty buffer for storing activity records.

This callback function signals the CUPTI client that an activity buffer is needed by CUPTI. The activity buffer is used by CUPTI to store activity records. The callback function can decline the request by setting `*buffer` to NULL. In this case CUPTI may drop activity records.

fields.Param buffer: Returns the new buffer. If set to NULL then no buffer is returned.
fields.Param size: Returns the size of the returned buffer.
fields.Param maxNumRecords: Returns the maximum number of records that should be placed in the buffer. If 0 then the buffer is filled with as many records as possible. If > 0 the buffer is filled with at most that many records before it is returned.
fields.Param pBufferRequestInfo: Additional information about the requested buffer.

CUpti_TimestampCallbackFunc.doc:
Function type for callback used by CUPTI to request a timestamp to be used in activity records.

This callback function signals the CUPTI client that a timestamp needs to be returned. This timestamp would be treated as normalized timestamp to be used for various purposes in CUPTI. For example to store start and end timestamps reported in the CUPTI activity records. The returned timestamp must be in nanoseconds.

See also

[cuptiActivityRegisterTimestampCallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gac168c4a9b5f4e9bd7553ca26118a307d).

CUPTI_OLD_SUBSCRIBER_NAME_MIN_LEN.doc: The minimum size of the of the old subscriber name in bytes.

CUPTI_SUBSCRIBER_NAME_MAX_LEN.doc:
The max size of the CUPTI subscriber name in bytes.

The total size of the CUPTI subscriber name is 64 bytes. CUPTI adds a 10 byte prefix and a null terminator, leaving 53 bytes for the user supplied subscriber name.

CUPTI_CBID_STATE_FATAL_ERROR.doc: Notification of fatal errors - high impact, non-recoverable When encountered, CUPTI automatically invokes [cuptiFinalize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gaad1be905ea718ed54246e52e02667e8f) User can control behavior of the application in future from receiving this callback - such as continuing without profiling, or terminating the whole application.

buffer.doc: The buffer to store the enabled callbacks. If NULL, the number of enabled callbacks is returned in `enabledCallbacksCount`.

bufferSize.doc: The size of the buffer. If NULL, only the number of enabled callbacks is returned in `enabledCallbacksCount`. If NULL and `buffer` is not NULL, [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`] is returned.

enabledCallbacksCount.doc: The number of enabled callbacks. If NULL, [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`] is returned.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `enabledCallbacksCount` is NULL, or if `subscriber` or `domain` is invalid.

cuptiSubscribe.signature: CUptiResult cuptiSubscribe(CUpti_SubscriberHandle * subscriber, CUpti_CallbackFunc callback, void * userdata)
cuptiSubscribe.doc:
Initialize a callback subscriber with a callback function and user data.

Initializes a callback subscriber with a callback function and (optionally) a pointer to user data. The returned subscriber handle can be used to enable and disable the callback for specific domains and callback IDs.

userdata.doc: A pointer to user data. This data will be passed to the callback function via the `userdata` parameter.

CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUP.doc: if there is already a CUPTI subscriber, or if the application is launched with NVIDIA tools like Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, cuda-gdb and cuda-memcheck.

cuptiSubscribe_v2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiSubscribe_v2(CUpti_SubscriberHandle * subscriber, CUpti_CallbackFunc callback, void * userdata, CUpti_SubscriberParams * pParams)
cuptiSubscribe_v2.doc:
Initialize a callback subscriber with a callback function and user data.

Initializes a callback subscriber with a callback function and (optionally) a pointer to user data. The returned subscriber handle can be used to enable and disable the callback for specific domains and callback IDs.

userdata.doc: A pointer to user data. This data will be passed to the callback function via the `userdata` parameter.

pParams.doc: A pointer to [CUpti_SubscriberParams](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__SubscriberParams.html#structcupti__subscriberparams). Can be NULL.

CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUP.doc: if there is already a CUPTI subscriber, or if the application is launched with NVIDIA tools like Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, cuda-gdb and cuda-memcheck.

- **CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER** \u20.doc:
**[`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`]** – if:
  * `pParams.structSize` is not filled with the size of the structure.

cuptiSupportedDomains.doc:
Get the available callback domains.

Returns in `*domainTable` an array of size `*domainCount` of all the available callback domains.

domainTable.doc: Returns pointer to array of available callback domains.

cuptiUnsubscribe.doc:
Unregister a callback subscriber.

Removes a callback subscriber so that no future callbacks will be issued to that subscriber.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `subscriber` is NULL or not initialized.

CUpti_CallbackFunc.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_CallbackFunc)(void * userdata, CUpti_CallbackDomain domain, CUpti_CallbackId cbid, const void * cbdata)
CUpti_CallbackFunc.doc:
Function type for a callback.

Function type for a callback. The type of the data passed to the callback in `cbdata` depends on the `domain`. If `domain` is [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_DRIVER_API`] or [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_RUNTIME_API`] the type of `cbdata` will be [CUpti_CallbackData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__CallbackData.html#structcupti__callbackdata). If `domain` is [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_RESOURCE`] the type of `cbdata` will be [CUpti_ResourceData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__ResourceData.html#structcupti__resourcedata). If `domain` is [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_SYNCHRONIZE`] the type of `cbdata` will be [CUpti_SynchronizeData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__SynchronizeData.html#structcupti__synchronizedata). If `domain` is [`CUpti_CallbackDomain::CUPTI_CB_DOMAIN_NVTX`] the type of `cbdata` will be [CUpti_NvtxData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__NvtxData.html#structcupti__nvtxdata).

fields.Param userdata: User data supplied at subscription of the callback

CUpti_CallbackId.doc:
An ID for a driver API, runtime API, resource or synchronization callback.

An ID for a driver API, runtime API, resource or synchronization callback. Within a driver API callback this should be interpreted as a CUpti_driver_api_trace_cbid value (these values are defined in cupti_driver_cbid.h). Within a runtime API callback this should be interpreted as a CUpti_runtime_api_trace_cbid value (these values are defined in cupti_runtime_cbid.h). Within a resource API callback this should be interpreted as a [CUpti_CallbackIdResource](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__CALLBACK__API.html#group__cupti__callback__api_1ga690fb2a42aefe39f00033c957ce211b2) value. Within a synchronize API callback this should be interpreted as a [CUpti_CallbackIdSync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__CALLBACK__API.html#group__cupti__callback__api_1gacaeba9950bf4f48ea7ab9a0402dc7e6f) value.

CUpti_DomainTable.doc: Pointer to an array of callback domains.

CUPTI_EVENT_INVALID.doc: The value that indicates the event value is invalid.

CUPTI_EVENT_OVERFLOW.doc:
The overflow value for a CUPTI event.

The CUPTI event value that indicates an overflow.

CUpti_DeviceAttribute.doc:
Device attributes.

CUPTI device attributes. These attributes can be read using [cuptiDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga631a8f494a7f0f3d254ad49f2040eff5).

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_MAX_EVENT_ID.doc:
Number of event IDs for a device.

Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_MAX_EVENT_DOMAIN_ID.doc:
Number of event domain IDs for a device.

Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_GLOBAL_MEMORY_BANDWIDT.doc:
Get global memory bandwidth in Kbytes/sec.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_INSTRUCTION_PER_CYCLE.doc:
Get theoretical maximum number of instructions per cycle.

Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_INSTRUCTION_THROUGHPUT.doc:
Get theoretical maximum number of single precision instructions that can be executed per second.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_MAX_FRAME_BUFFERS.doc:
Get number of frame buffers for device.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_PCIE_LINK_RATE.doc:
Get PCIE link rate in Mega bits/sec for device.

Return 0 if bus-type is non-PCIE. Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_PCIE_LINK_WIDTH.doc:
Get PCIE link width for device.

Return 0 if bus-type is non-PCIE. Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_PCIE_GEN.doc:
Get PCIE generation for device.

Return 0 if bus-type is non-PCIE. Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_DEVICE_CLASS.doc:
Get the class for the device.

Value is a CUpti_DeviceAttributeDeviceClass.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_FLOP_SP_PER_CYCLE.doc:
Get the peak single precision flop per cycle.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_FLOP_DP_PER_CYCLE.doc:
Get the peak double precision flop per cycle.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_MAX_L2_UNITS.doc:
Get number of L2 units.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_CACH.doc:
Get the maximum shared memory for the CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_SHARED preference.

Value is a uint64_t.

Get the maximum shared memory for the CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_L1 preference.

Value is a uint64_t.

Get the maximum shared memory for the CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_EQUAL preference.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_FLOP_HP_PER_CYCLE.doc:
Get the peak half precision flop per cycle.

Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_NVLINK_PRESENT.doc:
Check if Nvlink is connected to device.

Returns 1, if at least one Nvlink is connected to the device, returns 0 otherwise. Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_GPU_CPU_NVLINK_BW.doc:
Check if Nvlink is present between GPU and CPU.

Returns Bandwidth, in Bytes/sec, if Nvlink is present, returns 0 otherwise. Value is a uint64_t.

CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_NVSWITCH_PRESENT.doc:
Check if NVSwitch is present in the underlying topology.

Returns 1, if present, returns 0 otherwise. Value is a uint32_t.

CUpti_DeviceAttributeDeviceClass.doc:
Device class.

Enumeration of device classes for device attribute [`CUpti_DeviceAttribute::CUPTI_DEVICE_ATTR_DEVICE_CLASS`].

CUpti_EventAttribute.doc:
Event attributes.

Event attributes. These attributes can be read using [cuptiEventGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gaec3d52db48a14aef9e8b35785bb4d60e).

CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_NAME.doc:
Event name.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_SHORT_DESCRIPTION.doc:
Short description of event.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_LONG_DESCRIPTION.doc:
Long description of event.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_CATEGORY.doc:
Category of event.

Value is CUpti_EventCategory.

CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_PROFILING_SCOPE.doc:
Profiling scope of the events.

It can be either device or context or both. Value is a [CUpti_EventProfilingScope](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga5fbde5d55673e4d937491e6ea9631940).

CUpti_EventCategory.doc:
An event category.

Each event is assigned to a category that represents the general type of the event. A event’s category is accessed using [cuptiEventGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gaec3d52db48a14aef9e8b35785bb4d60e) and the [`CUpti_EventAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_ATTR_CATEGORY`] attribute.

CUpti_EventCollectionMethod.doc:
The collection method used for an event.

The collection method indicates how an event is collected.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_METHOD_PM.doc: Event is collected using a hardware global performance monitor.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_METHOD_SM.doc: Event is collected using a hardware SM performance monitor.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_METHOD_INSTRUMENT.doc: Event is collected using software instrumentation.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_METHOD_NVLINK_TC.doc: Event is collected using NvLink throughput counter method.

CUpti_EventCollectionMode.doc:
Event collection modes.

The event collection mode determines the period over which the events within the enabled event groups will be collected.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_MODE_CONTINUOUS.doc:
Events are collected for the entire duration between the cuptiEventGroupEnable and cuptiEventGroupDisable calls.

Event values are reset when the events are read. For CUDA toolkit v6.0 and older this was the default mode.

CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_MODE_KERNEL.doc:
Events are collected only for the durations of kernel executions that occur between the cuptiEventGroupEnable and cuptiEventGroupDisable calls.

Event collection begins when a kernel execution begins, and stops when kernel execution completes. Event values are reset to zero when each kernel execution begins. If multiple kernel executions occur between the cuptiEventGroupEnable and cuptiEventGroupDisable calls then the event values must be read after each kernel launch if those events need to be associated with the specific kernel launch. Note that collection in this mode may significantly change the overall performance characteristics of the application because kernel executions that occur between the cuptiEventGroupEnable and cuptiEventGroupDisable calls are serialized on the GPU. This is the default mode from CUDA toolkit v6.5.

CUpti_EventDomainAttribute.doc:
Event domain attributes.

Event domain attributes. Except where noted, all the attributes can be read using either [cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gabb745099ffef139c4ee98a1de82fcac2) or [cuptiEventDomainGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gaf8084beb1c692a17616fb99523a044a5).

CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_NAME.doc:
Event domain name.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT.doc:
Number of instances of the domain for which event counts will be collected.

The domain may have additional instances that cannot be profiled (see [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_TOTAL_INSTANCE_COUNT`]). Can be read only with [cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gabb745099ffef139c4ee98a1de82fcac2). Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_TOTAL_INSTANCE_C.doc:
Total number of instances of the domain, including instances that cannot be profiled.

Use [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT`] to get the number of instances that can be profiled. Can be read only with [cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gabb745099ffef139c4ee98a1de82fcac2). Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_COLLECTION_METHO.doc:
Collection method used for events contained in the event domain.

Value is a [CUpti_EventCollectionMethod](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gadafc575cd4614872eba5d99e2f2bc831).

CUpti_EventGroupAttribute.doc:
Event group attributes.

Event group attributes. These attributes can be read using [cuptiEventGroupGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga573c7e8a0295d36cf0051e27554971a8). Attributes marked [rw] can also be written using [cuptiEventGroupSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gadeea7eb4a79d3c7e85db597f2c98d5ac).

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_EVENT_DOMAIN_ID.doc:
The domain to which the event group is bound.

This attribute is set when the first event is added to the group. Value is a CUpti_EventDomainID.

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAI.doc:
[rw] Profile all the instances of the domain for this eventgroup.

This feature can be used to get load balancing across all instances of a domain. Value is an integer.

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_NUM_EVENTS.doc:
Number of events in the group.

Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_EVENTS.doc:
Enumerates events in the group.

Value is a pointer to buffer of size sizeof(CUpti_EventID) \* num_of_events in the eventgroup. num_of_events can be queried using [`CUpti_EventGroupAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_NUM_EVENTS`].

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT.doc:
Number of instances of the domain bound to this event group that will be counted.

Value is a uint32_t.

CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILING_SCOPE.doc:
Event group scope can be set to [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_DEVICE`] or [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_CONTEXT`] for an eventGroup, before adding any event.

Sets the scope of eventgroup as [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_DEVICE`] or [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_CONTEXT`] when the scope of the events that will be added is [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_BOTH`]. If profiling scope of event is either [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_DEVICE`] or [`CUpti_EventProfilingScope::CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_CONTEXT`] then setting this attribute will not affect the default scope. It is not allowed to add events of different scope to same eventgroup. Value is a uint32_t.

CUpti_EventProfilingScope.doc:
Profiling scope for event.

Profiling scope of event indicates if the event can be collected at context scope or device scope or both i.e. it can be collected at any of context or device scope.

CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_CONTEXT.doc: Event is collected at context scope.

CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_DEVICE.doc: Event is collected at device scope.

CUPTI_EVENT_PROFILING_SCOPE_BOTH.doc:
Event can be collected at device or context scope.

The scope can be set using [cuptiEventGroupSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gadeea7eb4a79d3c7e85db597f2c98d5ac) API.

CUpti_ReadEventFlags.doc:
Flags for cuptiEventGroupReadEvent an cuptiEventGroupReadAllEvents.

Flags for [cuptiEventGroupReadEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga31c30e2c86218a3501ae8a21127dec15) an [cuptiEventGroupReadAllEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gabb522fec20a70e3b5d8f819693c4f2dd).

cuptiDeviceEnumEventDomains.signature: CUptiResult cuptiDeviceEnumEventDomains(CUdevice device, size_t * arraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventDomainID * domainArray)
cuptiDeviceEnumEventDomains.doc:
Get the event domains for a device.

Returns the event domains IDs in `domainArray` for a device. The size of the `domainArray` buffer is given by `*arraySizeBytes`. The size of the `domainArray` buffer must be at least `numdomains` \* sizeof(CUpti_EventDomainID) or else all domains will not be returned. The value returned in `*arraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `domainArray`.

arraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `domainArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `domainArray`.

domainArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the event domains for the device.

cuptiDeviceGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiDeviceGetAttribute(CUdevice device, CUpti_DeviceAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiDeviceGetAttribute.doc:
Read a device attribute.

Read a device attribute and return it in `*value`.

valueSize.doc: Size of buffer pointed by the value, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

value.doc: Returns the value of the attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not a device attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute(CUdevice device, CUpti_EventDomainID eventDomain, CUpti_EventDomainAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiDeviceGetEventDomainAttribute.doc:
Read an event domain attribute.

Returns an event domain attribute in `*value`. The size of the `value` buffer is given by `*valueSize`. The value returned in `*valueSize` contains the number of bytes returned in `value`.

If the attribute value is a c-string that is longer than `*valueSize`, then only the first `*valueSize` characters will be returned and there will be no terminating null byte.

attrib.doc: The event domain attribute to read.

valueSize.doc: The size of the `value` buffer in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not an event domain attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiDeviceGetNumEventDomains.doc:
Get the number of domains for a device.

Returns the number of domains in `numDomains` for a device.

cuptiDisableKernelReplayMode.doc:
Disable kernel replay mode.

Set profiling mode for the context to non-replay (default) mode. Event collection mode will be set to [`CUpti_EventCollectionMode::CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_MODE_KERNEL`]. All previously enabled event groups and event group sets will be disabled.

cuptiEnableKernelReplayMode.doc:
Enable kernel replay mode.

Set profiling mode for the context to replay mode. In this mode, any number of events can be collected in one run of the kernel. The event collection mode will automatically switch to [`CUpti_EventCollectionMode::CUPTI_EVENT_COLLECTION_MODE_KERNEL`]. In this mode, [cuptiSetEventCollectionMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1gadfa8bf3fa3d6c6445f2cb874d0b54cf3) will return [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION`].

cuptiEnumEventDomains.doc:
Get the event domains available on any device.

Returns all the event domains available on any CUDA-capable device. Event domain IDs are returned in `domainArray`. The size of the `domainArray` buffer is given by `*arraySizeBytes`. The size of the `domainArray` buffer must be at least `numDomains` \* sizeof(CUpti_EventDomainID) or all domains will not be returned. The value returned in `*arraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `domainArray`.

arraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `domainArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `domainArray`.

cuptiEventDomainEnumEvents.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventDomainEnumEvents(CUpti_EventDomainID eventDomain, size_t * arraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventArray)
cuptiEventDomainEnumEvents.doc:
Get the events in a domain.

Returns the event IDs in `eventArray` for a domain. The size of the `eventArray` buffer is given by `*arraySizeBytes`. The size of the `eventArray` buffer must be at least `numdomainevents` \* sizeof(CUpti_EventID) or else all events will not be returned. The value returned in `*arraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `eventArray`.

arraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `eventArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `eventArray`.

eventArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the events in the domain.

cuptiEventDomainGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventDomainGetAttribute(CUpti_EventDomainID eventDomain, CUpti_EventDomainAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiEventDomainGetAttribute.doc:
Read an event domain attribute.

Returns an event domain attribute in `*value`. The size of the `value` buffer is given by `*valueSize`. The value returned in `*valueSize` contains the number of bytes returned in `value`.

If the attribute value is a c-string that is longer than `*valueSize`, then only the first `*valueSize` characters will be returned and there will be no terminating null byte.

attrib.doc: The event domain attribute to read.

valueSize.doc: The size of the `value` buffer in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not an event domain attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiEventDomainGetNumEvents.doc:
Get number of events in a domain.

Returns the number of events in `numEvents` for a domain.

numEvents.doc: Returns the number of events in the domain.

cuptiEventGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGetAttribute(CUpti_EventID event, CUpti_EventAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiEventGetAttribute.doc:
Get an event attribute.

Returns an event attribute in `*value`. The size of the `value` buffer is given by `*valueSize`. The value returned in `*valueSize` contains the number of bytes returned in `value`.

If the attribute value is a c-string that is longer than `*valueSize`, then only the first `*valueSize` characters will be returned and there will be no terminating null byte.

valueSize.doc: The size of the `value` buffer in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not an event attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiEventGetIdFromName.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGetIdFromName(CUdevice device, const char * eventName, CUpti_EventID * event)
cuptiEventGetIdFromName.doc:
Find an event by name.

Find an event by name and return the event ID in `*event`.

eventName.doc: The name of the event to find.

event.doc: Returns the ID of the found event or undefined if unable to find the event.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_EVENT_NAME.doc: if unable to find an event with name `eventName`. In this case `*event` is undefined.

cuptiEventGroupAddEvent.doc:
Add an event to an event group.

Add an event to an event group. The event add can fail for a number of reasons:

* The event group is enabled
* The event does not belong to the same event domain as the events that are already in the event group
* Device limitations on the events that can belong to the same group
* The event group is full.

event.doc: The event to add to the group.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if `eventGroup` is enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if `event` belongs to a different event domain than the events already in `eventGroup`, or if a device limitation prevents `event` from being collected at the same time as the events already in `eventGroup`.

cuptiEventGroupCreate.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupCreate(CUcontext context, CUpti_EventGroup * eventGroup, uint32_t flags)
cuptiEventGroupCreate.doc:
Create a new event group for a context.

Creates a new event group for `context` and returns the new group in `*eventGroup`.

context.doc: The context for the event group.

flags.doc: Reserved - must be zero.

cuptiEventGroupDestroy.doc:
Destroy an event group.

Destroy an `eventGroup` and free its resources. An event group cannot be destroyed if it is enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if the event group is enabled.

cuptiEventGroupDisable.doc:
Disable an event group.

Disable an event group. Disabling an event group stops collection of events contained in the group.

cuptiEventGroupEnable.doc:
Enable an event group.

Enable an event group. Enabling an event group zeros the value of all the events in the group and then starts collection of those events.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_READY.doc: if `eventGroup` does not contain any events.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if `eventGroup` cannot be enabled due to other already enabled event groups.

CUPTI_ERROR_HARDWARE_BUSY.doc: if another client is profiling and hardware is busy.

cuptiEventGroupGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupGetAttribute(CUpti_EventGroup eventGroup, CUpti_EventGroupAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiEventGroupGetAttribute.doc:
Read an event group attribute.

Read an event group attribute and return it in `*value`.

valueSize.doc: Size of buffer pointed by the value, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

value.doc: Returns the value of the attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not an eventgroup attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiEventGroupReadAllEvents.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupReadAllEvents(CUpti_EventGroup eventGroup, CUpti_ReadEventFlags flags, size_t * eventValueBufferSizeBytes, uint64_t * eventValueBuffer, size_t * eventIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventIdArray, size_t * numEventIdsRead)
cuptiEventGroupReadAllEvents.doc:
Read the values for all the events in an event group.

Read the values for all the events in an event group. The event values are returned in the `eventValueBuffer` buffer. `eventValueBufferSizeBytes` indicates the size of `eventValueBuffer`. The buffer must be at least (sizeof(uint64) \* number of events in group) if [CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggac8aaac37b2aefeea5177c0b813806b9fa776be3128e2ab834a96ec9ff16dda611) is not set on the group containing the events. The buffer must be at least (sizeof(uint64) \* number of domain instances \* number of events in group) if [CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggac8aaac37b2aefeea5177c0b813806b9fa776be3128e2ab834a96ec9ff16dda611) is set on the group.

The data format returned in `eventValueBuffer` is:

* domain instance 0: event0 event1 … eventN
* domain instance 1: event0 event1 … eventN
* …
* domain instance M: event0 event1 … eventN

The event order in `eventValueBuffer` is returned in `eventIdArray`. The size of `eventIdArray` is specified in `eventIdArraySizeBytes`. The size should be at least (sizeof(CUpti_EventID) \* number of events in group).

If any instance of any event counter overflows, the value returned for that event instance will be [CUPTI_EVENT_OVERFLOW](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga4f280929637a726da2ba4c907e5b9ba1).

The only allowed value for `flags` is [CUPTI_EVENT_READ_FLAG_NONE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggae8ea7de2653cc087a9c5399386604528a726bee26555027440a8b4acdf6ff13a3).

Reading events from a disabled event group is not allowed. After being read, an event’s value is reset to zero.

flags.doc: Flags controlling the reading mode.

eventValueBufferSizeBytes.doc: The size of `eventValueBuffer` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `eventValueBuffer`.

eventIdArraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `eventIdArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `eventIdArray`.

eventIdArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the events in the same order as the values return in eventValueBuffer.

numEventIdsRead.doc: Returns the number of event IDs returned in `eventIdArray`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if `eventGroup` is disabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: if size of `eventValueBuffer` or `eventIdArray` is not sufficient.

cuptiEventGroupReadEvent.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupReadEvent(CUpti_EventGroup eventGroup, CUpti_ReadEventFlags flags, CUpti_EventID event, size_t * eventValueBufferSizeBytes, uint64_t * eventValueBuffer)
cuptiEventGroupReadEvent.doc:
Read the value for an event in an event group.

Read the value for an event in an event group. The event value is returned in the `eventValueBuffer` buffer. `eventValueBufferSizeBytes` indicates the size of the `eventValueBuffer` buffer. The buffer must be at least sizeof(uint64) if [CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggac8aaac37b2aefeea5177c0b813806b9fa776be3128e2ab834a96ec9ff16dda611) is not set on the group containing the event. The buffer must be at least (sizeof(uint64) \* number of domain instances) if [CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggac8aaac37b2aefeea5177c0b813806b9fa776be3128e2ab834a96ec9ff16dda611) is set on the group.

If any instance of an event counter overflows, the value returned for that event instance will be [CUPTI_EVENT_OVERFLOW](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga4f280929637a726da2ba4c907e5b9ba1).

The only allowed value for `flags` is [CUPTI_EVENT_READ_FLAG_NONE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ggae8ea7de2653cc087a9c5399386604528a726bee26555027440a8b4acdf6ff13a3).

Reading an event from a disabled event group is not allowed. After being read, an event’s value is reset to zero.

flags.doc: Flags controlling the reading mode.

eventValueBufferSizeBytes.doc: The size of `eventValueBuffer` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `eventValueBuffer`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if `eventGroup` is disabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: if size of `eventValueBuffer` is not sufficient.

cuptiEventGroupRemoveAllEvents.doc:
Remove all events from an event group.

Remove all events from an event group. Events cannot be removed if the event group is enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if `eventGroup` is enabled.

cuptiEventGroupRemoveEvent.doc:
Remove an event from an event group.

Remove `event` from the an event group. The event cannot be removed if the event group is enabled.

event.doc: The event to remove from the group.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if `eventGroup` is enabled.

cuptiEventGroupResetAllEvents.doc:
Zero all the event counts in an event group.

Zero all the event counts in an event group.

cuptiEventGroupSetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupSetAttribute(CUpti_EventGroup eventGroup, CUpti_EventGroupAttribute attrib, size_t valueSize, void * value)
cuptiEventGroupSetAttribute.doc:
Write an event group attribute.

Write an event group attribute.

valueSize.doc: The size, in bytes, of the value.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not an event group attribute, or if `attrib` is not a writable attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: Indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiEventGroupSetDisable.doc:
Disable an event group set.

Disable a set of event groups. Disabling a set of event groups stops collection of events contained in the groups.

cuptiEventGroupSetEnable.doc:
Enable an event group set.

Enable a set of event groups. Enabling a set of event groups zeros the value of all the events in all the groups and then starts collection of those events.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_READY.doc: if `eventGroup` does not contain any events.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: if `eventGroup` cannot be enabled due to other already enabled event groups.

CUPTI_ERROR_HARDWARE_BUSY.doc: if other client is profiling and hardware is busy.

cuptiEventGroupSetsCreate.signature: CUptiResult cuptiEventGroupSetsCreate(CUcontext context, size_t eventIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventIdArray, CUpti_EventGroupSets * * eventGroupPasses)
cuptiEventGroupSetsCreate.doc:
For a set of events, get the grouping that indicates the number of passes and the event groups necessary to collect the events.

The number of events that can be collected simultaneously varies by device and by the type of the events. When events can be collected simultaneously, they may need to be grouped into multiple event groups because they are from different event domains. This function takes a set of events and determines how many passes are required to collect all those events, and which events can be collected simultaneously in each pass.

The [CUpti_EventGroupSets](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__EventGroupSets.html#structcupti__eventgroupsets) returned in `eventGroupPasses` indicates how many passes are required to collect the events with the `numSets` field. Within each event group set, the `sets` array indicates the event groups that should be collected on each pass.

eventIdArray.doc: Array of event IDs that need to be grouped.

eventGroupPasses.doc: Returns a [CUpti_EventGroupSets](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__EventGroupSets.html#structcupti__eventgroupsets) object that indicates the number of passes required to collect the events and the events to collect on each pass.

cuptiEventGroupSetsDestroy.doc:
Destroy a event group sets object.

Destroy a [CUpti_EventGroupSets](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__EventGroupSets.html#structcupti__eventgroupsets) object.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if any of the event groups contained in the sets is enabled.

cuptiGetNumEventDomains.doc:
Get the number of event domains available on any device.

Returns the total number of event domains available on any CUDA-capable device.

cuptiKernelReplaySubscribeUpdate.doc:
Subscribe to kernel replay updates.

When subscribed, the function pointer passed in will be called each time a kernel run is finished during kernel replay. Previously subscribed function pointer will be replaced. Pass in NULL as the function pointer unsubscribes the update.

cuptiSetEventCollectionMode.doc:
Set the event collection mode.

Set the event collection mode for a `context`. The `mode` controls the event collection behavior of all events in event groups created in the `context`. This API is invalid in kernel replay mode.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if called when replay mode is enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: if mode is not supported on the device.

CUpti_EventDomainID.doc:
ID for an event domain.

ID for an event domain. An event domain represents a group of related events. A device may have multiple instances of a domain, indicating that the device can simultaneously record multiple instances of each event within that domain.

CUpti_EventGroup.doc:
A group of events.

An event group is a collection of events that are managed together. All events in an event group must belong to the same domain.

CUpti_EventID.doc:
ID for an event.

An event represents a countable activity, action, or occurrence on the device.

CUpti_KernelReplayUpdateFunc.signature: typedef void(*CUpti_KernelReplayUpdateFunc)(const char * kernelName, int numReplaysDone, void * customData)
