fields.Param numReplaysDone: Number of replays done so far
fields.Param customData: Pointer of any custom data passed in when subscribing

CUpti_MetricAttribute.doc:
Metric attributes.

Metric attributes describe properties of a metric. These attributes can be read using [cuptiMetricGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaad77ae5441ca5c8cee0156b4ecc4d3f5).

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_NAME.doc:
Metric name.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_SHORT_DESCRIPTION.doc:
Short description of metric.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_LONG_DESCRIPTION.doc:
Long description of metric.

Value is a null terminated const c-string.

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_CATEGORY.doc:
Category of the metric.

Value is of type CUpti_MetricCategory.

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_VALUE_KIND.doc:
Value type of the metric.

Value is of type CUpti_MetricValueKind.

CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_EVALUATION_MODE.doc:
Metric evaluation mode.

Value is of type CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode.

CUpti_MetricCategory.doc:
A metric category.

Each metric is assigned to a category that represents the general type of the metric. A metric’s category is accessed using [cuptiMetricGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaad77ae5441ca5c8cee0156b4ecc4d3f5) and the [`CUpti_MetricAttribute::CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_CATEGORY`] attribute.

CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode.doc:
A metric evaluation mode.

A metric can be evaluated per hardware instance to know the load balancing across instances of a domain or the metric can be evaluated in aggregate mode when the events involved in metric evaluation are from different event domains. It might be possible to evaluate some metrics in both modes for convenience. A metric’s evaluation mode is accessed using [CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1ga59396bc237d98ee0595e5743bde89b9d) and the [`CUpti_MetricAttribute::CUPTI_METRIC_ATTR_EVALUATION_MODE`] attribute.

CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_PER_INSTANC.doc:
If this bit is set, the metric can be profiled for each instance of the domain.

The event values passed to [cuptiMetricGetValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaf42dcb1d349f91265e7809bbba2fc01e) can contain values for one instance of the domain. And [cuptiMetricGetValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaf42dcb1d349f91265e7809bbba2fc01e) can be called for each instance.

CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_AGGREGATE.doc:
If this bit is set, the metric can be profiled over all instances.

The event values passed to [cuptiMetricGetValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaf42dcb1d349f91265e7809bbba2fc01e) can be aggregated values of events for all instances of the domain.

CUpti_MetricPropertyDeviceClass.doc:
Device class.

Enumeration of device classes for metric property [`CUpti_MetricPropertyID::CUPTI_METRIC_PROPERTY_DEVICE_CLASS`].

CUpti_MetricPropertyID.doc:
Metric device properties.

Metric device properties describe device properties which are needed for a metric. Some of these properties can be collected using cuDeviceGetAttribute.

CUpti_MetricValueKind.doc:
Kinds of metric values.

Metric values can be one of several different kinds. Corresponding to each kind is a member of the [CUpti_MetricValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/unionCUpti__MetricValue.html#unioncupti__metricvalue) union. The metric value returned by [cuptiMetricGetValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1gaf42dcb1d349f91265e7809bbba2fc01e) should be accessed using the appropriate member of that union based on its value kind.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_DOUBLE.doc: The metric value is a 64-bit double.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_UINT64.doc: The metric value is a 64-bit unsigned integer.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_PERCENT.doc:
The metric value is a percentage represented by a 64-bit double.

For example, 57.5% is represented by the value 57.5.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_THROUGHPUT.doc:
The metric value is a throughput represented by a 64-bit integer.

The unit for throughput values is bytes/second.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_INT64.doc: The metric value is a 64-bit signed integer.

CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_UTILIZATION_LEVE.doc: The metric value is a utilization level, as represented by CUpti_MetricValueUtilizationLevel.

CUpti_MetricValueUtilizationLevel.doc:
Enumeration of utilization levels for metrics values of kind [`CUpti_MetricValueKind::CUPTI_METRIC_VALUE_KIND_UTILIZATION_LEVEL`].

Utilization values can vary from IDLE (0) to MAX (10) but the enumeration only provides specific names for a few values.

cuptiDeviceEnumMetrics.signature: CUptiResult cuptiDeviceEnumMetrics(CUdevice device, size_t * arraySizeBytes, CUpti_MetricID * metricArray)
cuptiDeviceEnumMetrics.doc:
Get the metrics for a device.

Returns the metric IDs in `metricArray` for a device. The size of the `metricArray` buffer is given by `*arraySizeBytes`. The size of the `metricArray` buffer must be at least `numMetrics` \* sizeof(CUpti_MetricID) or else all metric IDs will not be returned. The value returned in `*arraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `metricArray`.

arraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `metricArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `metricArray`.

metricArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the metrics for the device.

cuptiDeviceGetNumMetrics.doc:
Get the number of metrics for a device.

Returns the number of metrics available for a device.

numMetrics.doc: Returns the number of metrics available for the device.

cuptiEnumMetrics.doc:
Get all the metrics available on any device.

Returns the metric IDs in `metricArray` for all CUDA-capable devices. The size of the `metricArray` buffer is given by `*arraySizeBytes`. The size of the `metricArray` buffer must be at least `numMetrics` \* sizeof(CUpti_MetricID) or all metric IDs will not be returned. The value returned in `*arraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `metricArray`.

arraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `metricArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `metricArray`.

metricArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the metrics.

cuptiGetNumMetrics.doc:
Get the total number of metrics available on any device.

Returns the total number of metrics available on any CUDA-capable devices.

cuptiMetricCreateEventGroupSets.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricCreateEventGroupSets(CUcontext context, size_t metricIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_MetricID * metricIdArray, CUpti_EventGroupSets * * eventGroupPasses)
cuptiMetricCreateEventGroupSets.doc:
For a set of metrics, get the grouping that indicates the number of passes and the event groups necessary to collect the events required for those metrics.

[cuptiEventGroupSetsCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__EVENT__API.html#group__cupti__event__api_1ga0fd307d429d4e37f61f45472de069910) for details on event group set creation.

cuptiMetricEnumEvents.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricEnumEvents(CUpti_MetricID metric, size_t * eventIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventIdArray)
cuptiMetricEnumEvents.doc:
Get the events required to calculating a metric.

Gets the event IDs in `eventIdArray` required to calculate a `metric`. The size of the `eventIdArray` buffer is given by `*eventIdArraySizeBytes` and must be at least `numEvents` \* sizeof(CUpti_EventID) or all events will not be returned. The value returned in `*eventIdArraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `eventIdArray`.

eventIdArraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `eventIdArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `eventIdArray`.

eventIdArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the events required to calculate `metric`.

cuptiMetricEnumProperties.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricEnumProperties(CUpti_MetricID metric, size_t * propIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_MetricPropertyID * propIdArray)
cuptiMetricEnumProperties.doc:
Get the properties required to calculating a metric.

Gets the property IDs in `propIdArray` required to calculate a `metric`. The size of the `propIdArray` buffer is given by `*propIdArraySizeBytes` and must be at least `numProp` \* sizeof(CUpti_DeviceAttribute) or all properties will not be returned. The value returned in `*propIdArraySizeBytes` contains the number of bytes returned in `propIdArray`.

propIdArraySizeBytes.doc: The size of `propIdArray` in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `propIdArray`.

propIdArray.doc: Returns the IDs of the properties required to calculate `metric`.

cuptiMetricGetAttribute.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricGetAttribute(CUpti_MetricID metric, CUpti_MetricAttribute attrib, size_t * valueSize, void * value)
cuptiMetricGetAttribute.doc:
Get a metric attribute.

Returns a metric attribute in `*value`. The size of the `value` buffer is given by `*valueSize`. The value returned in `*valueSize` contains the number of bytes returned in `value`.

If the attribute value is a c-string that is longer than `*valueSize`, then only the first `*valueSize` characters will be returned and there will be no terminating null byte.

valueSize.doc: The size of the `value` buffer in bytes, and returns the number of bytes written to `value`.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `valueSize` or `value` is NULL, or if `attrib` is not a metric attribute.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: For non-c-string attribute values, indicates that the `value` buffer is too small to hold the attribute value.

cuptiMetricGetIdFromName.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricGetIdFromName(CUdevice device, const char * metricName, CUpti_MetricID * metric)
cuptiMetricGetIdFromName.doc:
Find an metric by name.

Find a metric by name and return the metric ID in `*metric`.

metricName.doc: The name of metric to find.

metric.doc: Returns the ID of the found metric or undefined if unable to find the metric.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_METRIC_NAME.doc: if unable to find a metric with name `metricName`. In this case `*metric` is undefined.

cuptiMetricGetNumEvents.doc:
Get number of events required to calculate a metric.

Returns the number of events in `numEvents` that are required to calculate a metric.

numEvents.doc: Returns the number of events required for the metric.

cuptiMetricGetNumProperties.doc:
Get number of properties required to calculate a metric.

Returns the number of properties in `numProp` that are required to calculate a metric.

numProp.doc: Returns the number of properties required for the metric.

cuptiMetricGetRequiredEventGroupSets.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricGetRequiredEventGroupSets(CUcontext context, CUpti_MetricID metric, CUpti_EventGroupSets * * eventGroupSets)
cuptiMetricGetRequiredEventGroupSets.doc:
For a metric get the groups of events that must be collected in the same pass.

For a metric get the groups of events that must be collected in the same pass to ensure that the metric is calculated correctly. If the events are not collected as specified then the metric value may be inaccurate.

The function returns NULL if a metric does not have any required event group. In this case the events needed for the metric can be grouped in any manner for collection.

eventGroupSets.doc: Returns a [CUpti_EventGroupSets](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__EventGroupSets.html#structcupti__eventgroupsets) object that indicates the events that must be collected in the same pass to ensure the metric is calculated correctly. Returns NULL if no grouping is required for metric.

cuptiMetricGetValue.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricGetValue(CUdevice device, CUpti_MetricID metric, size_t eventIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventIdArray, size_t eventValueArraySizeBytes, uint64_t * eventValueArray, uint64_t timeDuration, CUpti_MetricValue * metricValue)
cuptiMetricGetValue.doc:
Calculate the value for a metric.

Use the events collected for a metric to calculate the metric value. Metric value evaluation depends on the evaluation mode [CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1ga59396bc237d98ee0595e5743bde89b9d) that the metric supports. If a metric has evaluation mode as [`CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode::CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_PER_INSTANCE`], then it assumes that the input event value is for one domain instance. If a metric has evaluation mode as [`CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode::CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_AGGREGATE`], it assumes that input event values are normalized to represent all domain instances on a device. For the most accurate metric collection, the events required for the metric should be collected for all profiled domain instances. For example, to collect all instances of an event, set the [`CUpti_EventGroupAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES`] attribute on the group containing the event to 1. The normalized value for the event is then: (`sum_event_values` \* `totalInstanceCount`) / `instanceCount`, where `sum_event_values` is the summation of the event values across all profiled domain instances, `totalInstanceCount` is obtained from querying [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_TOTAL_INSTANCE_COUNT`] and `instanceCount` is obtained from querying [`CUpti_EventGroupAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT`] (or [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT`]).

device.doc: The CUDA device that the metric is being calculated for.

eventIdArray.doc: The event IDs required to calculate `metric`.

eventValueArray.doc: The normalized event values required to calculate `metric`. The values must be order to match the order of events in `eventIdArray`.

timeDuration.doc: The duration over which the events were collected, in ns.

metricValue.doc: Returns the value for the metric.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: if the eventIdArray does not contain all the events needed for metric.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_EVENT_VALUE.doc: if any of the event values required for the metric is CUPTI_EVENT_OVERFLOW.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_METRIC_VALUE.doc: if the computed metric value cannot be represented in the metric’s value type. For example, if the metric value type is unsigned and the computed metric value is negative.

cuptiMetricGetValue2.signature: CUptiResult cuptiMetricGetValue2(CUpti_MetricID metric, size_t eventIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_EventID * eventIdArray, size_t eventValueArraySizeBytes, uint64_t * eventValueArray, size_t propIdArraySizeBytes, CUpti_MetricPropertyID * propIdArray, size_t propValueArraySizeBytes, uint64_t * propValueArray, CUpti_MetricValue * metricValue)
cuptiMetricGetValue2.doc:
Calculate the value for a metric.

Use the events and properties collected for a metric to calculate the metric value. Metric value evaluation depends on the evaluation mode [CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__METRIC__API.html#group__cupti__metric__api_1ga59396bc237d98ee0595e5743bde89b9d) that the metric supports. If a metric has evaluation mode as [`CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode::CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_PER_INSTANCE`], then it assumes that the input event value is for one domain instance. If a metric has evaluation mode as [`CUpti_MetricEvaluationMode::CUPTI_METRIC_EVALUATION_MODE_AGGREGATE`], it assumes that input event values are normalized to represent all domain instances on a device. For the most accurate metric collection, the events required for the metric should be collected for all profiled domain instances. For example, to collect all instances of an event, set the [`CUpti_EventGroupAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_PROFILE_ALL_DOMAIN_INSTANCES`] attribute on the group containing the event to 1. The normalized value for the event is then: (`sum_event_values` \* `totalInstanceCount`) / `instanceCount`, where `sum_event_values` is the summation of the event values across all profiled domain instances, `totalInstanceCount` is obtained from querying [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_TOTAL_INSTANCE_COUNT`] and `instanceCount` is obtained from querying [`CUpti_EventGroupAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_GROUP_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT`] (or [`CUpti_EventDomainAttribute::CUPTI_EVENT_DOMAIN_ATTR_INSTANCE_COUNT`]).

eventIdArray.doc: The event IDs required to calculate `metric`.

eventValueArray.doc: The normalized event values required to calculate `metric`. The values must be order to match the order of events in `eventIdArray`.

propIdArray.doc: The metric property IDs required to calculate `metric`.

propValueArray.doc: The metric property values required to calculate `metric`. The values must be order to match the order of metric properties in `propIdArray`.

metricValue.doc: Returns the value for the metric.

CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYP.doc:
[rw] Sampling period for PC Sampling.

DEFAULT - CUPTI defined value based on number of SMs Valid values for the sampling periods are between 5 to 31 both inclusive. This will set the sampling period to (2^samplingPeriod) cycles. For e.g. for sampling period = 5 to 31, cycles = 32, 64, 128,…, 2^31 Value is a uint32_t.

[w] Number of stall reasons to collect.

DEFAULT - All stall reasons will be collected Value is a size_t [w] Stall reasons to collect DEFAULT - All stall reasons will be collected Input value should be a pointer pointing to array of stall reason indexes containing all the stall reason indexes to collect.

[rw] Size of SW buffer for raw PC counter data downloaded from HW buffer DEFAULT - 1 MB, which can accommodate approximately 5500 PCs with all stall reasons Approximately it takes 16 Bytes (and some fixed size memory) to accommodate one PC with one stall reason For e.g.

1 PC with 1 stall reason = 32 Bytes 1 PC with 2 stall reason = 48 Bytes 1 PC with 4 stall reason = 96 Bytes Value is a size_t.
[rw] Size of HW buffer in bytes DEFAULT - 512 MB If sampling period is too less, HW buffer can overflow and drop PC data Value is a size_t.

[rw] PC Sampling collection mode DEFAULT - [`CUpti_PCSamplingCollectionMode::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_COLLECTION_MODE_CONTINUOUS`] Input value should be of type [CUpti_PCSamplingCollectionMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga7fcaa834e5520b282b2a3b1de3f304b4).

[rw] Control over PC Sampling data collection range Default - 0 1 - Allows user to start and stop PC Sampling using APIs - [cuptiPCSamplingStart()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga569d99977964b8f7b0f771a153666a6f) - Start PC Sampling [cuptiPCSamplingStop()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga942cf8284013fe62b61d5988e6c1052f) - Stop PC Sampling Value is a uint32_t.

[w] Value for output data format Default - [`CUpti_PCSamplingOutputDataFormat::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_OUTPUT_DATA_FORMAT_PARSED`] Input value should be of type [CUpti_PCSamplingOutputDataFormat](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga6959d5af9fa0ce5b41af09276fc190f7).

[w] Data buffer to hold collected PC Sampling data PARSED_DATA Default - none.

Buffer type is void \* which can point to PARSED_DATA Refer [CUpti_PCSamplingData](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__PCSamplingData.html#structcupti__pcsamplingdata) for buffer format for PARSED_DATA.

[rw] Control sleep time of the worker threads created by CUPTI for various PC sampling operations.

CUPTI creates multiple worker threads to offload certain operations to these threads. This includes decoding of HW data to the CUPTI PC sampling data and correlating PC data to SASS instructions. CUPTI wakes up these threads periodically. Default - 100 milliseconds. Value is a uint32_t.

cuptiPCSamplingGetData.doc:
Flush GPU PC sampling data periodically.

Flushing of GPU PC Sampling data is required at following point to maintain uniqueness of PCs: For [`CUpti_PCSamplingCollectionMode::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_COLLECTION_MODE_CONTINUOUS`], after every module load-unload-load For [`CUpti_PCSamplingCollectionMode::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_COLLECTION_MODE_KERNEL_SERIALIZED`], after every kernel ends If configuration option [`CUpti_PCSamplingConfigurationAttributeType::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYPE_ENABLE_START_STOP_CONTROL`] is enabled, then after every range end i.e. [cuptiPCSamplingStop()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga942cf8284013fe62b61d5988e6c1052f)

If application is profiled in [`CUpti_PCSamplingCollectionMode::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_COLLECTION_MODE_CONTINUOUS`], with disabled

[`CUpti_PCSamplingConfigurationAttributeType::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYPE_ENABLE_START_STOP_CONTROL`], and there is no module unload, user can collect data in two ways: Use [cuptiPCSamplingGetData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga6a34245ee39a52a31e231845af598e6b) API periodically Use [cuptiPCSamplingDisable()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1gacbe97deb69ca2795102902544df571e3) on application exit and read GPU PC sampling data from sampling data buffer passed during configuration. Note: In case, [cuptiPCSamplingGetData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga6a34245ee39a52a31e231845af598e6b) API is not called periodically, then sampling data buffer passed during configuration should be large enough to hold all PCs data.

[cuptiPCSamplingGetData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PCSAMPLING__API.html#group__cupti__pcsampling__api_1ga6a34245ee39a52a31e231845af598e6b) API never does device synchronization. It is possible that when the API is called there is some unconsumed data from the HW buffer. In this case CUPTI provides only the data available with it at that moment.

Add the metrics to the profiler host object for generating the config image.

The config image will have the required information to schedule the metrics for collecting the profiling data. Note:

* PM sampling only supports single pass config image.
* CUPTI has single pass sets supported for a chip, all metrics in a set can be collected in a single pass.
* [cuptiProfilerHostGetSinglePassSets](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__HOST__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__host__api_1gaef29112ebeaf0bf683f5ed5539e6c357) API can be used to get the single pass sets supported for a chip.

cuptiProfilerHostGetMetricsInSinglePassS.doc:
Get all the metrics defined in the single pass metric set.

Profiling data for the metrics in a single pass metric set can be collected in a single pass.

This is a two-phase function to retrieve metrics in a single-pass metric set. First pass (query mode): Set pParams->pMetricsBuffer = NULL and pParams->pMetricsIndicesBuffer = NULL The function returns required buffer sizes in:

* numOfMetricsInSinglePassSet: Number of metrics in set
* metricsBufferSize: Total buffer size needed for metric data

Second pass (data retrieval):

* Set pParams->pMetricsBuffer = allocated buffer for metrics
* Set pParams->pMetricsIndicesBuffer = allocated buffer for metrics indices
* Set pParams->numOfMetricsInSinglePassSet = number of metrics in set
* Set pParams->metricsBufferSize = allocated buffer size for metrics
* Call the function again to populate the buffers.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if any `pParams` is not valid also when either of pMetricsBuffer and pMetricsIndicesBuffer are NULL while the other is not NULL.

cuptiProfilerHostSetDevicePartitionInfo.doc:
Set the device partition information for metric evaluation on Green Contexts.

When profiling workloads running on Green Contexts, the device resources (such as Streaming Multiprocessors) are partitioned among multiple Green Contexts. This partition information is essential for correctly evaluating and scaling metric values from the collected counter data.

The device partition information should be obtained from the target side using [cuptiRangeProfilerGetDevicePartitionInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__RANGE__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__range__profiler__api_1ga5bc20e82550fba23fc3fc6caba8363ab) after starting the range profiler on a Green Context. This information must be set on the profiler host object before calling [cuptiProfilerHostEvaluateToGpuValues](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__HOST__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__host__api_1ga388a983e8bcfc889721c17aae2e67a4f) to ensure accurate metric evaluation that accounts for the partitioned device resources.

Note: This API is only required when profiling on Green Contexts. For profiling on regular CUDA contexts that have access to all device resources, this API is not needed.

CUpti_ProfilerRange.doc:
Profiler range attribute.

A metric enabled in the session’s configuration is collected separately per unique range-stack in the pass. This is an attribute to collect metrics around each kernel in a profiling session or in an user defined range.

CUPTI_AutoRange.doc: Ranges are auto defined around each kernel in a profiling session.

CUPTI_UserRange.doc: A range in which metric data to be collected is defined by the user.

For metrics which require multipass collection, a replay of the GPU kernel(s) is required. This is an attribute which specify how the replay of the kernel(s) to be measured is done.

CUPTI_ApplicationReplay.doc: Replay is done by CUPTI user around the process.

CUPTI_KernelReplay.doc: Replay is done around kernel implicitly by CUPTI.

CUPTI_UserReplay.doc: Replay is done by CUPTI user within a process.

Replay API: used for multipass collection.

These APIs are used if user chooses to replay by itself [CUPTI_UserReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457aa052699f076ad798166b7b653b0ce14e) or [CUPTI_ApplicationReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457a298b65c9526dabe7113fdb5b9e45c957) for multipass collection of the metrics configurations. It’s a no-op in case of [CUPTI_KernelReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457ac2e3d8f8e8ad65399ae39f6d0e266bc8).

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerBeginSession.doc:
Begin profiling session sets up the profiling on the device.

Although, it doesn’t start the profiling but GPU resources needed for profiling are allocated. Outside of a session, the GPU will return to its normal operating state.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerCounterDataImageCalculateSc.doc:
A temporary storage for CounterData image needed for internal operations.

Use these APIs to calculate the allocation size and initialize counterData image scratch buffer.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerCounterDataImageCalculateSi.doc:
A CounterData image allocates space for values for each counter for each range.

User borne the resposibility of managing the counterDataImage allocations. CounterDataPrefix contains meta data about the metrics that will be stored in counterDataImage. Use these APIs to calculate the allocation size and initialize counterData image.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerDeviceSupported.doc:
Query device compatibility with Profiling API.

Use this call to determine whether a compute device and configuration are compatible with the Profiling API. If the configuration does not support profiling, one of several flags will indicate why.

cuptiProfilerDisableProfiling.doc:
Disable Profiling.

In [CUPTI_AutoRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggaa6faef578b53da403b15878e05d1b395aee196550a6a859439d2a4aa4ab531cf0), these APIs are used to enable/disable profiling for the kernels to be executed in a profiling session.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerEnableProfiling.doc:
Enables Profiling.

In [CUPTI_AutoRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggaa6faef578b53da403b15878e05d1b395aee196550a6a859439d2a4aa4ab531cf0), these APIs are used to enable/disable profiling for the kernels to be executed in a profiling session.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerEndPass.doc:
Replay API: used for multipass collection.

These APIs are used if user chooses to replay by itself [CUPTI_UserReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457aa052699f076ad798166b7b653b0ce14e) or [CUPTI_ApplicationReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457a298b65c9526dabe7113fdb5b9e45c957) for multipass collection of the metrics configurations. Its a no-op in case of [CUPTI_KernelReplay](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggad6960f26de20f317a784ee565743e457ac2e3d8f8e8ad65399ae39f6d0e266bc8). Returns information for next pass.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerEndSession.doc:
Ends profiling session.

Frees up the GPU resources acquired for profiling. Outside of a session, the GPU will return to it’s normal operating state.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerFlushCounterData.doc:
Decode all the submitted passes.

Flush Counter data API to ensure every pass is decoded into the counterDataImage passed at beginSession. This will cause the CPU/GPU sync to collect all the undecoded pass.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerGetCounterAvailability.doc:
Query counter availibility.

Use this API to query counter availability information in a buffer which can be used to filter unavailable raw metrics on host. Note: This API may fail, if any profiling or sampling session is active on the specified context or its device.

cuptiProfilerInitialize.doc:
Initializes the profiler interface.

Loads the required libraries in the process address space. Sets up the hooks with the CUDA driver.

cuptiProfilerIsPassCollected.doc:
Asynchronous call to query if the submitted pass to GPU is collected.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerPopRange.doc:
Range API’s : Pop user range.

Counter data is collected per unique range-stack. Identified by a string label passsed by the user. It’s an invalid operation in case of [CUPTI_AutoRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggaa6faef578b53da403b15878e05d1b395aee196550a6a859439d2a4aa4ab531cf0).

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerPushRange.doc:
Range API’s : Push user range.

Counter data is collected per unique range-stack. Identified by a string label passsed by the user. It’s an invalid operation in case of [CUPTI_AutoRange](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__api_1ggaa6faef578b53da403b15878e05d1b395aee196550a6a859439d2a4aa4ab531cf0).

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiProfilerSetConfig.doc:
Set metrics configuration to be profiled.

Use these APIs to set the config to profile in a session. It can be used for advanced cases such as where multiple configurations are collected into a single CounterData Image on the need basis, without restarting the session.

**DEPRECATED**.

cuptiRangeProfilerCounterDataGetRangeInf.doc: Get the range name for the given range index.

cuptiRangeProfilerCounterDataImageInitia.doc: Initialize the counter data image with the profiling data for the ranges profiled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler CounterDataImageInitialize is called without enabling range profiler.

cuptiRangeProfilerDecodeData.doc:
Decode the profiling data stored in the hardware to the counter data image passed in the SetConfig API.

This API should be called after cuptiRangeProfilerStop. The counter data image will be updated with the profiling data for the ranges profiled.

For the cases where the number of ranges counter data image can store is less than the number of ranges profiled (= maxRangesPerPass in SetConfig API), the counter data image will report dropped ranges.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler DecodeData is called without enabling range profiler.

cuptiRangeProfilerDisable.doc: Disable the range profiler on the CUDA context and destroy the range profiler object.

cuptiRangeProfilerEnable.doc: Create a range profiler object and enable range profiling on the CUDA context.

CUPTI_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY.doc: if memory allocation fails while creating the PM sampling object.

CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES.doc: if the user does not have sufficient privileges to perform the operation.

cuptiRangeProfilerGetCounterDataInfo.doc: Get the number of ranges stored in the counter data image.

cuptiRangeProfilerGetCounterDataSize.doc: Get the size of the counter data image required to store the profiling data for the ranges profiled.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler GetCounterDataSize is called without enabling range profiler.

cuptiRangeProfilerGetDevicePartitionInfo.doc:
Get the device partition information for a Green Context.

Green Contexts are created by partitioning device resources such as Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) using CUDA APIs like cuDevSmResourceSplitByCount and cuGreenCtxCreate. When range profiling is enabled on a Green Context, the device partition information encodes how the device resources are divided among the Green Contexts.

This API retrieves the device partition information from the range profiler object, which is required for accurate metric evaluation on the host side. The retrieved partition information should be passed to [cuptiProfilerHostSetDevicePartitionInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__HOST__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__host__api_1gae2acff2140fd3cdfbd91f47b8db1c1b8) before evaluating metrics using [cuptiProfilerHostEvaluateToGpuValues](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__PROFILER__HOST__API.html#group__cupti__profiler__host__api_1ga388a983e8bcfc889721c17aae2e67a4f). This API needs to be called after [cuptiRangeProfilerStart](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__RANGE__PROFILER__API.html#group__cupti__range__profiler__api_1gaae839f931a50f1436df35367e3e71416).

This is a two-phase function:

* First call: Set `pDevicePartitionInfo` to NULL to query the required buffer size. The required size is returned in `devicePartitionInfoSize`.
* Second call: Allocate a buffer of the returned size and set `pDevicePartitionInfo` to point to it. Set `devicePartitionInfoSize` to the allocated buffer size. The function populates the buffer with the device partition information.

cuptiRangeProfilerPopRange.doc:
pop the current range to the Range Profiler.

The number of pop range API call should be same as number of push ranges in the same order.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler PopRange is called without enabling range profiler.

cuptiRangeProfilerPushRange.doc:
Add a new range to the Range Profiler with a given range name.

For nested ranges, this API should be called again for the innermost range. For profiling the nested range, users need to set the values for minNestingLevel and numNestingLevels in the SetConfig API.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler PushRange is called without enabling range profiler.

cuptiRangeProfilerSetConfig.doc: Set the configuration for range profiler like maximum number of ranges per pass, number of nesting levels, range and replay mode and the config image which has scheduling info for metric collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if range profiler Start is called without enabling range profiler.
if range profiler Stop is called without enabling range profiler.

CUptiResult.doc:
CUPTI result codes.

Error and result codes returned by CUPTI functions.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: One or more of the parameters is invalid.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE.doc: The device does not correspond to a valid CUDA device.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc: The context is NULL or not valid.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_EVENT_DOMAIN_ID.doc: The event domain id is invalid.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: The current operation cannot be performed due to dependency on other factors.

CUPTI_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY.doc: Unable to allocate enough memory to perform the requested operation.

CUPTI_ERROR_HARDWARE.doc: An error occurred on the performance monitoring hardware.

CUPTI_ERROR_PARAMETER_SIZE_NOT_SUFFICIEN.doc: The output buffer size is not sufficient to return all requested data.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_READY.doc: The object is not yet ready to perform the requested operation.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc: The current operation is not compatible with the current state of the object.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: CUPTI is unable to initialize its connection to the CUDA driver.

CUPTI_ERROR_DISABLED.doc: CUPTI is disabled due to conflicts with other enabled profilers.

CUPTI_ERROR_HARDWARE_BUSY.doc: The performance monitoring hardware is in use by other client.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: The attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

CUPTI_ERROR_UM_PROFILING_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc:
Unified memory profiling is not supported on the system.

Potential reason could be unsupported OS or architecture.

CUPTI_ERROR_UM_PROFILING_NOT_SUPPORTED_O.doc: Unified memory profiling is not supported on the device.
Unified memory profiling is not supported on a multi-GPU configuration without P2P support between any pair of devices.

CUPTI_ERROR_UM_PROFILING_NOT_SUPPORTED_W.doc:
Unified memory profiling is not supported under the Multi-Process Service (MPS) environment.

CUDA 7.5 removes this restriction.

CUPTI_ERROR_CDP_TRACING_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: In CUDA 9.0, devices with compute capability 7.0 don’t support CDP tracing.

CUPTI_ERROR_VIRTUALIZED_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPO.doc: Profiling on virtualized GPU is not supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_CUDA_COMPILER_NOT_COMPATIBLE.doc:
Profiling results might be incorrect for CUDA applications compiled with nvcc version older than 9.0 for devices with compute capability 6.0 and 6.1.

Profiling session will continue and CUPTI will notify it using this error code. User is advised to recompile the application code with nvcc version 9.0 or later. Ignore this warning if code is already compiled with the recommended nvcc version.

CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES.doc:
User doesn’t have sufficient privileges which are required to start the profiling session.

One possible reason for this may be that the NVIDIA driver or your system administrator may have restricted access to the NVIDIA GPU performance counters. To learn how to resolve this issue and find more information, please visit <https://developer.nvidia.com/[`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES`]>.

CUPTI_ERROR_OLD_PROFILER_API_INITIALIZED.doc:
Legacy CUPTI Profiling API i.e.

event API from the header cupti_events.h and metric API from the header cupti_metrics.h are not compatible with the Profiling API in the header cupti_profiler_target.h and Perfworks metrics API in the headers nvperf_host.h and nvperf_target.h.

CUPTI_ERROR_OPENACC_UNDEFINED_ROUTINE.doc:
Missing definition of the OpenACC API routine in the linked OpenACC library.

One possible reason is that OpenACC library is linked statically in the user application, which might not have the definition of all the OpenACC API routines needed for the OpenACC profiling, as compiler might ignore definitions for the functions not used in the application. This issue can be mitigated by linking the OpenACC library dynamically.

CUPTI_ERROR_LEGACY_PROFILER_NOT_SUPPORTE.doc:
Legacy CUPTI Profiling API i.e.

event API from the header cupti_events.h and metric API from the header cupti_metrics.h are not supported on devices with compute capability 7.5 and higher (i.e. Turing and later GPU architectures). These APIs were deprecated in CUDA 12.8 and removed in CUDA 13.0. These are replaced by the host profiling API in the header cupti_profiler_host.h and target profiling API in the header cupti_range_profiler.h which are supported on devices with compute capability 7.5 and higher (i.e. Turing and later GPU architectures). Further, the PC Sampling Activity API and the source/SASS level metrics from the header cupti_activity.h are removed in CUDA 13.0.

CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUP.doc:
CUPTI doesn’t allow multiple callback subscribers.

Only a single subscriber can be registered at a time. Same error code is used when application is launched using NVIDIA tools like Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, and cuda-gdb.

CUPTI_ERROR_VIRTUALIZED_DEVICE_INSUFFICI.doc: Profiling on virtualized GPU is not allowed by hypervisor.

CUPTI_ERROR_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTING_NOT_S.doc: Profiling and tracing are not allowed when confidential computing mode is enabled.

CUPTI_ERROR_CMP_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc:
CUPTI does not support NVIDIA Crypto Mining Processors (CMP).

For more information, please visit <https://developer.nvidia.com/ERR_NVCMPGPU>.

CUPTI_ERROR_MIG_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: Profiling on Multi-instance GPU (MIG) is not supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_SLI_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: Profiling on SLI device is not supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_WSL_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: Profiling on WSL device is not supported.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CHIP_NAME.doc: For invalid or unsupported chip name passed to cuptiProfilerHostInitialize.

CUPTI_ERROR_HES_TRACE_NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_M.doc: Hardware Event System (HES) trace is not supported on MPS.

CUPTI_ERROR_UNKNOWN.doc: An unknown internal error has occurred.

cuptiGetErrorMessage.signature: CUptiResult cuptiGetErrorMessage(CUptiResult result, const char * * str)
cuptiGetErrorMessage.doc:
Get the descriptive message corresponding to error codes returned by CUPTI.

Return the descriptive error message for a CUptiResult in `*str`.

result.doc: The result to get the descriptive error message for.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `str` is NULL or `result` is not a valid CUptiResult.

cuptiGetResultString.signature: CUptiResult cuptiGetResultString(CUptiResult result, const char * * str)
cuptiGetResultString.doc:
Get the descriptive string for a CUptiResult.

Return the descriptive string for a CUptiResult in `*str`.

result.doc: The result to get the string for.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.doc: if `str` is NULL or `result` is not a valid CUptiResult.

CUPTI_SASS_METRICS_OUTPUT_GRANULARITY_GP.doc: SASS metric data will be collected at GPU level. In [CUpti_SassMetricsGetDataProperties_Params](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__SassMetricsGetDataProperties__Params.html#structcupti__sassmetricsgetdataproperties__params) struct the numOfInstances will be equal to 1.

CUPTI_SASS_METRICS_OUTPUT_GRANULARITY_SM.doc: SASS metric data will be collected at SM level In [CUpti_SassMetricsGetDataProperties_Params](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__SassMetricsGetDataProperties__Params.html#structcupti__sassmetricsgetdataproperties__params) struct the numOfInstances will be equal to number of SMs in the GPU.

SASS metric data will be collected at SM sub-partition level In [CUpti_SassMetricsGetDataProperties_Params](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__SassMetricsGetDataProperties__Params.html#structcupti__sassmetricsgetdataproperties__params) struct the numOfInstances will be equal to number of SM sub-partitions in the GPU.

cuptiSassMetricsDisable.doc: SASS metric data collection disable API will mark the end of a range, any kernel launched after this API call will not be profiled for the SASS metrics.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc: if any cuda context has not been created prior to this API call.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this API is called multiple times for a cuda context without calling [cuptiSassMetricsEnable()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga62ea0db81c966ddf066c28644f8b240f) API or called before [cuptiSassMetricsSetConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga0c3e83b6fa0938f8da75bea89092f848) API call.

cuptiSassMetricsEnable.doc: Sass metric data collection enable API will mark the start of a range, between which kernel will be profiled for SASS metrics.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc: if any cuda context has not been created prior to this API call.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this API is called multiple times for a cuda context without calling [cuptiSassMetricsDisable()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1gadf8447d381211251c69cdaf3221a5fec) API or called before [cuptiSassMetricsSetConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga0c3e83b6fa0938f8da75bea89092f848) API call.

cuptiSassMetricsFlushData.doc:
Flush SASS metrics data from CUPTI internal buffer to the user buffer.

User needs to allocate the buffer for retrieving the data. The number of records collected can be queried using the API [cuptiSassMetricsGetDataProperties()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga2601b1a5b4fe4b9253cdb81f04120b1e).

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this API is called outside the enable/disable range.

cuptiSassMetricsGetDataProperties.doc:
SASS metric data properties API will give the data regarding number of instances of a metric value and number of SASS instruction data has been collected.

The number of instances of a metric will vary as per user set the output granularity level with CUpti_SassMetrics_OutputGranularity value. User need to allocate memory for retriving the SASS data using [cuptiSassMetricsFlushData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga17d012eec574a36a7a8724177ba5e356) API.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this API is called outside the enable/disable range.

cuptiSassMetricsGetMetrics.doc: Get the list of all supported SASS metrics for the chip.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric collection.

cuptiSassMetricsGetNumOfMetrics.doc: Get the number of supported SASS metrics for the chip.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric collection.

cuptiSassMetricsGetProperties.doc:
Get metric properties for the queried metric.

For a given metric the results will be put in CUpti_SassMetrics_MetricDetails which stores metric ID, description of the metric.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

cuptiSassMetricsSetConfig.doc:
Set config for the SASS metric data collection for a device.

User need to call this API before calling any of the SASS metric data collection APIs. Each set config API call need to be followed by cuptiSassPatchingUnSetConfig API before calling the [cuptiSassMetricsSetConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga0c3e83b6fa0938f8da75bea89092f848) API again for the same device.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc: if any cuda context has not been created prior to this API call.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this is called multiple times for the device without calling unset config API.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

cuptiSassMetricsUnsetConfig.doc:
Unset config API will reset the SASS metric data collection configuration for the device.

Once this API called CUPTI will deallocate all the memory allocated and remove all the configuration for SASS metric data collection. User can only call this API for a device where [cuptiSassMetricsSetConfig()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__SASS__METRICS__API.html#group__cupti__sass__metrics__api_1ga0c3e83b6fa0938f8da75bea89092f848) API has been called earlier for the device.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc: if any cuda context has not been created prior to this API call.

CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION.doc: if this is called multiple times for the device without calling set config API.

CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: indicates that the system/device doesn’t support SASS metric data collection.

CUPTI_API_VERSION.doc:
The API version for this implementation of CUPTI.

The API version for this implementation of CUPTI. This define along with [cuptiGetVersion](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__VERSION__API.html#group__cupti__version__api_1ga0e63a0d235c5e7e5231cc78ec63fa981) can be used to dynamically detect if the version of CUPTI compiled against matches the version of the loaded CUPTI library.

v1 : CUDAToolsSDK 4.0 v2 : CUDAToolsSDK 4.1 v3 : CUDA Toolkit 5.0 v4 : CUDA Toolkit 5.5 v5 : CUDA Toolkit 6.0 v6 : CUDA Toolkit 6.5 v7 : CUDA Toolkit 6.5(with sm_52 support) v8 : CUDA Toolkit 7.0 v9 : CUDA Toolkit 8.0 v10 : CUDA Toolkit 9.0 v11 : CUDA Toolkit 9.1 v12 : CUDA Toolkit 10.0, 10.1 and 10.2 v13 : CUDA Toolkit 11.0 v14 : CUDA Toolkit 11.1 v15 : CUDA Toolkit 11.2, 11.3 and 11.4 v16 : CUDA Toolkit 11.5 v17 : CUDA Toolkit 11.6 v18 : CUDA Toolkit 11.8 v19 : CUDA Toolkit 12.0 v20 : CUDA Toolkit 12.2 v21 : CUDA Toolkit 12.3 v22 : CUDA Toolkit 12.4 v23 : CUDA Toolkit 12.5 v24 : CUDA Toolkit 12.6 v26 : CUDA Toolkit 12.8 v27 : CUDA Toolkit 12.9 v28 : CUDA Toolkit 12.9 Update 1

Starting with CUDA Toolkit 13.0, the CUPTI API version uses the format: xxyyzz where:

* xx : Major version of the CUDA Toolkit (e.g., 13 for CUDA 13.x)
* yy : Minor version of the CUDA Toolkit (e.g., 00 for 13.0, 01 for 13.1)
* zz : CUPTI-specific update or patch version (Note: This does NOT necessarily match the CUDA Toolkit update version)

Important:

* The CUPTI API version (CUPTI_API_VERSION) is distinct from CUDA_VERSION and CUDA_RUNTIME_VERSION.

v130000 : CUDA Toolkit 13.0 v130001 : CUDA Toolkit 13.0 with CUPTI update 1 v130100 : CUDA Toolkit 13.1 v130101 : CUDA Toolkit 13.1 with CUPTI update 1 v130200 : CUDA Toolkit 13.2 v130201 : CUDA Toolkit 13.2 with CUPTI update 1 v130300 : CUDA Toolkit 13.3.

cuptiGetVersion.doc:
Get the CUPTI API version.

Return the API version in `*version`.

See also

[CUPTI_API_VERSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__VERSION__API.html#group__cupti__version__api_1ga162a01934e005491e65643ca63dbf6a3).

CUpti_ActivityPCSamplingRecordInfo.doc:
The activity record for record status for PC sampling.

This activity records information obtained by sampling PC ([`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_PC_SAMPLING_RECORD_INFO`]).

kind.doc: The activity record kind, must be [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_PC_SAMPLING_RECORD_INFO`].

correlationId.doc: The correlation ID of the kernel to which this result is associated.

totalSamples.doc: Number of times the PC was sampled for this kernel instance including all dropped samples.

droppedSamples.doc: Number of samples that were dropped by hardware due to backpressure/overflow.

CUpti_ActivityKernel12.doc:
The activity record for kernel (version 12).

This activity record represents a kernel execution ([`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL`] and [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL`])

This version adds execution model for the kernel function.

requested.doc:
The cache configuration requested by the kernel.

The value is one of the CUfunc_cache enumeration values from cuda.h.

executed.doc:
The cache configuration used for the kernel.

The value is one of the CUfunc_cache enumeration values from cuda.h.

cacheConfig.doc: For devices with compute capability 7.5+ cacheConfig values are not updated in case field isSharedMemoryCarveoutRequested is set.

sharedMemoryConfig.doc:
The shared memory configuration used for the kernel.

The value is one of the CUsharedconfig enumeration values from cuda.h.

registersPerThread.doc: The number of registers required for each thread executing the kernel.

partitionedGlobalCacheRequested.doc:
The partitioned global caching requested for the kernel.

Partitioned global caching is required to enable caching on certain chips, such as devices with compute capability 5.2.

partitionedGlobalCacheExecuted.doc:
The partitioned global caching executed for the kernel.

Partitioned global caching is required to enable caching on certain chips, such as devices with compute capability 5.2. Partitioned global caching can be automatically disabled if the occupancy requirement of the launch cannot support caching.

start.doc:
The start timestamp for the kernel execution, in ns.

A value of 0 for both the start and end timestamps indicates that timestamp information could not be collected for the kernel.

end.doc:
The end timestamp for the kernel execution, in ns.

A value of 0 for both the start and end timestamps indicates that timestamp information could not be collected for the kernel.

completed.doc:
The completed timestamp for the kernel execution, in ns.

It represents the completion of all it’s child kernels and the kernel itself. A value of CUPTI_TIMESTAMP_UNKNOWN indicates that the completion time is unknown.

deviceId.doc: The ID of the device where the kernel is executing.

contextId.doc: The ID of the context where the kernel is executing.

streamId.doc: The ID of the stream where the kernel is executing.

gridX.doc: The X-dimension grid size for the kernel.

gridY.doc: The Y-dimension grid size for the kernel.

gridZ.doc: The Z-dimension grid size for the kernel.

blockX.doc: The X-dimension block size for the kernel.

blockY.doc: The Y-dimension block size for the kernel.

blockZ.doc: The Z-dimension grid size for the kernel.

staticSharedMemory.doc: The static shared memory allocated for the kernel, in bytes.

dynamicSharedMemory.doc: The dynamic shared memory reserved for the kernel, in bytes.

The total amount of local memory reserved for the kernel, in bytes (deprecated in CUDA 11.8).

Refer field localMemoryTotal_v2.

correlationId.doc:
The correlation ID of the kernel.

Each kernel execution is assigned a unique correlation ID that is identical to the correlation ID in the driver or runtime API activity record that launched the kernel.

gridId.doc:
The grid ID of the kernel.

Each kernel is assigned a unique grid ID at runtime.

name.doc:
The name of the kernel.

This name is shared across all activity records representing the same kernel, and so should not be modified.

queued.doc:
The timestamp when the kernel is queued up in the command buffer, in ns.

A value of CUPTI_TIMESTAMP_UNKNOWN indicates that the queued time could not be collected for the kernel. This timestamp is not collected by default. Use API [cuptiActivityEnableLatencyTimestamps()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga4b50c0c1634913f8157cfcfe84f19fa9) to enable collection.

Command buffer is a buffer written by CUDA driver to send commands like kernel launch, memory copy etc to the GPU. All launches of CUDA kernels are asynchronous with respect to the host, the host requests the launch by writing commands into the command buffer, then returns without checking the GPU’s progress.

submitted.doc:
The timestamp when the command buffer containing the kernel launch is submitted to the GPU, in ns.

A value of CUPTI_TIMESTAMP_UNKNOWN indicates that the submitted time could not be collected for the kernel. This timestamp is not collected by default. Use API [cuptiActivityEnableLatencyTimestamps()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga4b50c0c1634913f8157cfcfe84f19fa9) to enable collection.

launchType.doc:

The value will be updated only if field isSharedMemoryCarveoutRequested is set.

sharedMemoryExecuted.doc: Shared memory size set by the driver.
