Command buffer is a buffer written by CUDA driver to send commands like kernel launch, memory copy etc to the GPU. All launches of CUDA kernels are asynchronous with respect to the host, the host requests the launch by writing commands into the command buffer, then returns without checking the GPU’s progress.

submitted.doc:
The timestamp when the command buffer containing the kernel launch is submitted to the GPU, in ns.

A value of CUPTI_TIMESTAMP_UNKNOWN indicates that the submitted time could not be collected for the kernel. This timestamp is not collected by default. Use API [cuptiActivityEnableLatencyTimestamps()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1ga4b50c0c1634913f8157cfcfe84f19fa9) to enable collection.

launchType.doc:
The indicates if the kernel was executed via a regular launch or via a single/multi device cooperative launch.

See also

[CUpti_ActivityLaunchType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/group__CUPTI__ACTIVITY__API.html#group__cupti__activity__api_1gad054e12847a4a5a0ece53d2cb6dc6d8c).

isSharedMemoryCarveoutRequested.doc: This indicates if CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_SHARED_MEMORY_CARVEOUT was updated for the kernel launch.

sharedMemoryCarveoutRequested.doc:
Shared memory carveout value requested for the function in percentage of the total resource.

The value will be updated only if field isSharedMemoryCarveoutRequested is set.

sharedMemoryExecuted.doc: Shared memory size set by the driver.

graphNodeId.doc:
The unique ID of the graph node that launched this kernel through graph launch APIs.

This field will be 0 if the kernel is not launched through graph launch APIs.

shmemLimitConfig.doc:
The shared memory limit config for the kernel.

This field shows whether user has opted for a higher per block limit of dynamic shared memory.

graphId.doc:
The unique ID of the graph that launched this kernel through graph launch APIs.

This field will be 0 if the kernel is not launched through graph launch APIs.

pAccessPolicyWindow.doc:
The pointer to the access policy window.

The structure CUaccessPolicyWindow is defined in cuda.h.

channelID.doc: The ID of the HW channel on which the kernel is launched.

clusterX.doc:
The X-dimension cluster size for the kernel.

Field is valid for devices with compute capability 9.0 and higher.

clusterY.doc:
The Y-dimension cluster size for the kernel.

Field is valid for devices with compute capability 9.0 and higher.

clusterZ.doc:
The Z-dimension cluster size for the kernel.

Field is valid for devices with compute capability 9.0 and higher.

clusterSchedulingPolicy.doc:
The cluster scheduling policy for the kernel.

Refer CUclusterSchedulingPolicy Field is valid for devices with compute capability 9.0 and higher.

localMemoryTotal_v2.doc: The total amount of local memory reserved for the kernel, in bytes.

ctx.doc: [in] if NULL, the current CUcontext is used.

size.doc:
[w] Size of the data structure.

CUPTI client should set the size of the structure. It will be used in CUPTI to check what fields are available in the structure. Used to preserve backward compatibility.

collectNumPcs.doc: [w] Number of PCs to be collected.

totalSamples.doc:
[r] Number of samples collected across all PCs.

It includes samples for user modules, samples for non-user kernels and dropped samples. It includes counts for all non selected stall reasons. CUPTI does not provide PC records for non-user kernels. CUPTI does not provide PC records for instructions for which all selected stall reason metrics counts are zero.

droppedSamples.doc: [r] Number of samples that were dropped by hardware due to backpressure/overflow.

remainingNumPcs.doc: [r] Number of PCs available for collection.

rangeId.doc:
[r] Unique identifier for each range.

Data collected across multiple ranges in multiple buffers can be identified using range id.

pPcData.doc:
[r] Profiled PC data This data struct should have enough memory to collect number of PCs mentioned in

collectNumPcs.

nonUsrKernelsTotalSamples.doc:
[r] Number of samples collected across all non user kernels PCs.

It includes samples for non-user kernels. It includes counts for all non selected stall reasons as well. CUPTI does not provide PC records for non-user kernels.

hardwareBufferFull.doc:
[r] Status of the hardware buffer.

CUPTI returns the error code [`CUptiResult::CUPTI_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`] when hardware buffer is full. When hardware buffer is full, user will get pc data as 0. To mitigate this issue, one or more of the below options can be tried:

1. Increase the hardware buffer size using the attribute [`CUpti_PCSamplingConfigurationAttributeType::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYPE_HARDWARE_BUFFER_SIZE`]
2. Decrease the thread sleep span using the attribute [`CUpti_PCSamplingConfigurationAttributeType::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYPE_WORKER_THREAD_PERIODIC_SLEEP_SPAN`]
3. Decrease the sampling frequency using the attribute [`CUpti_PCSamplingConfigurationAttributeType::CUPTI_PC_SAMPLING_CONFIGURATION_ATTR_TYPE_SAMPLING_PERIOD`].

fanSpeed.doc: The fan speed as percentage of maximum.

CUpti_ActivitySynchronization.doc:
The activity record for synchronization management.

This activity is used to track various CUDA synchronization APIs. ([`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_SYNCHRONIZATION`]).

Structure deprecated in CUDA 12.8: Refer to [CUpti_ActivitySynchronization2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cupti/api/structCUpti__ActivitySynchronization2.html#structcupti__activitysynchronization2) for the latest structure.

kind.doc: The activity record kind, must be [`CUpti_ActivityKind::CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_SYNCHRONIZATION`].

start.doc:
The start timestamp for the function, in ns.

A value of 0 for both the start and end timestamps indicates that timestamp information could not be collected for the function.

end.doc:
The end timestamp for the function, in ns.

A value of 0 for both the start and end timestamps indicates that timestamp information could not be collected for the function.

correlationId.doc: The correlation ID of the API to which this result is associated.

contextId.doc:
The ID of the context for which the synchronization API is called.

In case of context synchronization API it is the context id for which the API is called. In case of stream/event synchronization it is the ID of the context where the stream/event was created.

streamId.doc:
The compute stream for which the synchronization API is called.

A CUPTI_SYNCHRONIZATION_INVALID_VALUE value indicate the field is not applicable for this record. Not valid for cuCtxSynchronize, cuEventSynchronize.

cudaEventId.doc:
The event ID for which the synchronization API is called.

A CUPTI_SYNCHRONIZATION_INVALID_VALUE value indicate the field is not applicable for this record. Not valid for cuCtxSynchronize, cuStreamSynchronize.
